The others are named for their topic (`timers`, `money`…).

**A name in question:** `bun exact.mjs contract vocab` prints the card, or read `docs/card.md` (the same
text): every function, tag, part's call, test step, and how to do a screen, sheet, timer, colour,
data, test. A lookup is for a name the card lacks or a compile error;
`docs/contract-for-agents.md` and `reference.md` by section (`bun exact.mjs docs tabular numbers`
prints one with its path and line); `apps/shelf` is a whole app.

## One screen: the view, its data, its test

`app.contract` is the view, `app.ts` its data module, `app.test.contract` its tests. A
screen is a route: its `header` the iOS navigation bar (the Mac window's title and toolbar) over the `scroll` its
`navigationScroll` names (`one-screen`; more screens: `contract vocab screen`). A location's
fragment is the same screen: `/item/7#moves` opens at its `id="moves"` once its data has arrived,
and a `link href="#moves"` goes there. Every host, the web
too, hides a stack's covered routes itself (not the page under a sheet, nor a wide split's list
beside its detail); `for e in stack(nav)` keeps them mounted with their scroll, which `[top(nav)]`
loses. A query follows the path:
`` path("home") + `?q=${v}` ``. This list takes the scroll's place:

```contract
shape Item
  id: string
  title: string
  done: bool

shape Reply
  ok: bool
  error: string

fn leftText(n: number): string = `${n} ${n == 1 ? "item" : "items"} left`

component Groceries
  state draft = ""
  resource groceries = loadItems() as shape Item[] else empty()
  mutation added as shape Reply refreshes groceries then afterAdd
  mutation saved as shape Reply queue refreshes groceries
  derive left = groceries.filter(i => not i.done).length
  derive addError = match added { case some(r) => r.error, case none => "" }

  action edit(v: string)
    draft = v
  action add
    if draft.trim() != ""
      send added = addItem(draft.trim())
  action afterAdd
    if addError == ""
      draft = ""
  action toggle(id: string, done: bool)
    send saved = setDone(id, done)

  view
    list id="items" appearance="auto" listStyle="inset-grouped" flex=1 min-height=0 testId="app"
      section
        row gap=8 align-items="center"
          column flex=1 min-width=0 gap=4
            input value=draft input=edit submit=add placeholder="Add an item"
              aria-label="New item" testId="draft"
            if addError != "" and not pending(added)
              text addError font="-exact-footnote" color="-exact-system-red" testId="add-error"
          button press=add disabled=(draft.trim() == "") buttonStyle="filled" testId="add"
            text "Add"
      section
        for i in groceries key=i.id
          row
            input type="checkbox" checked=i.done change=toggle(i.id) aria-label=i.title testId=`done-${i.id}`
            text i.title flex=1
        footer
          text (groceries.length == 0 ? "Nothing on the list." : leftText(left)) testId="left"
```

- **Styles.** A colour behind a box is `background-color`; the `background` shorthand is refused.
- **Syntax.** Indent with spaces. Quote units (`width="50%"`); a bare number is pixels.
  Subtract with spaces (`a - b`): names hold hyphens. A view chooses with `if`/`else`, as
  an action does, and repeats with `for x in xs key=x.id` (`for x, i in xs key=x.id` binds the
  index `i` too); no `form` (a field's Enter is its `submit`).
- **Fields.** An `input` handler should update the draft on every edit so live search,
  validation and button enablement follow typing. A text field fires `change` on Enter or
  blur; its handler should normalize the draft. Use `submit` for explicit submission.
- **Expressions** are TypeScript's: what compiles means what it means in TypeScript, and
  what does not is refused with what to write. The web's string and array methods are
  methods (`s.trim()`, `xs.filter(x => …)`, `xs.length`); the rest are functions
  (`first(xs)`, `round(n)`). What differs: no truthiness; absence is an option (`none`,
  `some(x)`, `match`), not `null`; a value never changes (`xs.concat([x])`, a record copy
  `Shape(old, field=value)`); `==` compares lists and records by value; a stored number is
  finite (a `NaN` refuses the commit). A presentation order by one key is
  `sortBy(xs, x => x.name)`, stable (`"desc"` third; a second key is an earlier `sortBy`), not
  `sort`; grouping, joining and a stored or locale order are the data module's, and the view
  names the order it relies on where it reads it (`resource tasks = loadTasksByDueDate()`).
  Nothing runs because a value changed: an event runs an action, which passes its captured
  arguments, then the payload (`toggle(i.id)` gets the bool). Its writes land when it ends, so a
  later line reads the old value: bind the new one (`let n = go(nav, url)`, `nav = n`, read `n`).
- **Data.** A `resource` is a reactive read (`pending(x)`, `failed(x)`); a `mutation` a
  write (`queue` keeps them in order, `refreshes` re-reads, `then` runs an action: clear
  the field only on an ok reply, as `afterAdd` does). Only the root declares them;
  children take `props`. For a mutation without `queue`, the action that sends it must
  not also assign its slot to `none`: assignments commit after sends and can discard its
  new reply. Hide an old error with `pending(added)`. `none` means the slot contains no
  reply, not failure; use `failure(added)` to show request failures and match the reply
  to handle a domain refusal.
- **Refreshes.** Include every resource the write changes (`refreshes groceries, counts`).

**The data module** answers each source with exactly its declared shape: an extra
field fails a resource or voids a mutation’s reply, whose slot keeps its old value.
Type the function returning a reply (`Promise<Result<'post'>>`) so the build names
an extra field. It reaches only what its `grants` name. A value fixed at build, such as an
API's origin, is `const API = import.meta.env.API_BASE_URL` at its top level, the name declared
in `app.json`'s `env` ([rest-backend](recipes/rest-backend.md)). A failed read should
fail its resource so Exact can retain its previous answer; a mutation may return
a shaped domain refusal for its action to handle
([fetch-loading-error](recipes/fetch-loading-error.md)). The clock and
randomness are refused there; time comes as an argument. A date from a value
works (`new Date(ms)`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`). `console.log` appears in the agent’s
`logs` and its last lines in a failed test’s notes. It imports its own `.ts`/`.js` and pure-JS npm
packages (ESM or CommonJS, a `browser` build first); one needing Node (`fs`, `Buffer`), the DOM or a native
addon is refused by name. Type an untyped one with `@types/<name>` or `declare module '<name>';` in a `.d.ts`.

```ts
import type { Answer, Result, Sources, Storage } from './app.contract.d.ts';

export const grants = 'fs.read app:/data/items.json\nfs.write app:/data/items.json';

type Item = Result<'loadItems'>[number];
const FILE = 'app:/data/items.json';
const load = (storage: Storage): Promise<Item[]> => storage.fs.readFile(FILE).then(
  (bytes) => JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes)),
  (e) => { if (e.code === 'ENOENT') return []; throw e; }); // no file yet ('bake', the build, passes)
const save = async (storage: Storage, items: Item[]) => {
  await storage.fs.atomicWriteFile(FILE, new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(items)));
  return { ok: true, error: '' };
};

const sources: Sources = {
  loadItems: (_args, _store, storage) => load(storage),
  addItem: async ([title], _store, storage) => {
    const all = await load(storage), same = all.find((i) => i.title.toLowerCase() === title.toLowerCase());
    if (same) return { ok: false, error: `${same.title} is already on the list.` }; // a refusal is a reply too
    return save(storage, [...all, { id: String(all.length + 1), title, done: false }]);
  },
  setDone: async ([id, done], _store, storage) => save(storage, (await load(storage)).map((i) => (i.id === id ? { ...i, done } : i))),
};
export const answer: Answer = (source, args, store, storage, native) => sources[source](args, store, storage, native);
```

Every step, launch line and `verify` flag is on the card.

Interactive web drives also accept `reload` (keeps storage and fetch faults) and
`pick <input-id> <path>`. `agent web --help all` lists driver capabilities.

Each mutation source request adds one millisecond of UI virtual time after the
step, including timer mutations issued during that advance. Reads and
continuations add none; arguments within an atomic action keep its clock
snapshot. The backend’s clock stays its own.

| To assert | Write | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A node is there, or not | `expect tree has "<testId>"`, `expect tree missing "<testId>"` | `lacks`, `contains`, `not has`. It matches a `testId` only, never a label or text, unlike `tap` |
| A node's text | `expect text "<testId>" == "the whole text"` | `contains`, `!=`. The text is compared whole, and a node with no text of its own reads its descendants' joined: a row's testId reads its buttons' labels too, so put the testId on the text node |
| State | `expect state lib.notes.0.title == "Milk"` (two list indexes in a row take a space: `grid.0 .1`; a drive's `clock until state` takes the same path), `== []`, `== none`, `== true` | an expression on the right |
| A failed resource or mutation request | `expect text` on the view's `match failure(x) { case some(f) => f.code, case none => "" }`; `failed(x)` accepts either slot | `failure(x).code` without extracting the option. A thrown refusal is a request failure; an authored `{ok: false}` is a normal result |

## Pitfalls that cost the most

1. **Styling a platform control.** Paint (`background-color`, `border`, `font-size`)
   on a `button`, field or bar makes it your box. Emphasis is a part (above) or
   `buttonStyle="filled"` on the screen's main action. A `button` with no
   `buttonStyle` is the platform's: tinted text on iOS, so one that must read as a
   button there says `"bordered"`, and Cancel or Edit says nothing. A field on its own is
   the platform's bordered one; a document's own text (a note's title and body, as Notes
   draws them) says `border="none"`, and a chat's composer is `chat-thread`'s.
2. **A `header` holds a heading (`h1 "Title"`), one text after it (the subtitle) and
   buttons** (or a search field, a `tablist`); anything else isn't in the iOS bar. A
   control fixed under the bar goes with an inline title (`h2`); one that may scroll
   away, in the list's first section.
3. **`width="100%"` with padding overflows**, as in CSS: drop the width; a `flex=1` field
   takes `min-width=0`.

Consecutive `match` blocks in an action all run in order. Nest a match in the
selected arm, or use `if`/`else`, for exclusive paths. Action reads still see
the state from the action’s start.

# Start here: building an app with Exact

The only required reading; the rest is lookup. A website reads [start-here-site.md](start-here-site.md) instead.

## The idea

1. **Write the web, ship the platform.** Layout and names are CSS's and HTML's (flex, gap,
   `role`, `aria-*`). Say what a thing *is* (a `header` with a heading and
   buttons, a `tablist`, a `dialog role="alertdialog"`); each host draws its own control.
   A data table is HTML's `table` (`thead`, `tr`, `th scope="col"`, `td colspan=2`), terms and their descriptions a `dl` (`dt`, `dd`).
2. **Leave the rest unsaid:** controls, bars, type and dark mode are the platform's, and so
   are a `list`'s rows: its children are rows, so draw no separator and no press. A
   colour or size names a role (`-exact-secondary-label`, `font="-exact-footnote"`; `bun
   <exact2>/scripts/no-tells.mjs .` lists literals). Leave the accent unsaid: it is the
   platform's blue, and a filled button keeps its white label (a pale accent under
   it is warned, `tamber-contrast`). A brand is an `app.tamber`; a colour names a role or
   one of its tokens, `color="ink"` or `color="var(--ink)"` (`recipes/tamber.md`). A card
   is `-exact-secondary-background` (`-exact-secondary-grouped-background` on a grouped page).
3. **Design your content:** a focal point (big type, a fill, a shape), a hierarchy in
   rows, an empty state with its next step in the list's place. A labelled entry or settings
   form is a grouped list (`grouped-form`), not cards of fields; a focal result (a timer, a
   converter's answer) stays a centred column (`max-width="26.25rem"`) or a `SummaryCard`.
   `use X from "exact:content"` draws them; the card gives each one's call (`none` for an option):
   - `RoundButton`: Start, Stop. `AnswerTile`: a choice; `status` is `"idle"`, `"selected"`,
     `"correct"`, `"wrong"`, `"dimmed"` or `"chosen"` (your pick once closed). `SummaryCard`: the one number, shown once
   - `RingProgress`, `StatBar`, `RowText`, `Badge` a status, `DoneMark` done or not; `EmptyState` with your `button` indented under it
4. **Compose as the platform does:** a row pushes its detail; create and edit are sheets; a
   phone gets one column, a wide window two (`responsive-columns`). Every screen, tab, detail
   and sheet is a route (`routes`, `push`, a row that is a `link href=path(…)`): on the web
   that is its URL, so Back, reload, a shared link and a new tab work, and focus moves to the
   new screen. A screen chosen by `if page == …` over a state has none of these, and the
   build warns (`lower-screen-by-state`). Tabs (a sidebar) and a
   list whose rows push (beside its detail) need no code. The rows of a list the person deletes from swipe to
   delete and open a menu on a long press (`list-detail`, `contract vocab swipe`).
   `haptic("selection")` marks a choice in your own control, `haptic("success")` a task done.
   A chat's messages are bubbles in a transcript that opens at the newest and follows each
   new one, not a grouped list's rows (`chat-thread`).

## The workflow

```sh
bun <exact2>/scripts/exact.mjs new ~/groceries && cd ~/groceries
bun exact.mjs pattern      # lists the starters; `pattern <name>` writes one
bun exact.mjs ios --prebuild  # the first iOS build: minutes, in the background; it names iOS in app.json
```

Start from the nearest pattern. The screen `exact new` writes, and its tests in
`app.test.contract`, are placeholders: replace both. `exact.mjs` runs from any
directory: a file you name is found where you are, else in the app, and it says
which it took. Your shell commands have no such help, so keep one directory.
|`bun exact.mjs …`|What it does|
|---|---|
|`contract build app.contract --json --errors-only`|A CI gate: `[]` and exit zero mean no errors (omit `--errors-only` to include warnings); it rewrites the types `app.ts` imports and type-checks it.|
|`verify`, `verify ios`|Builds, runs `app.test.contract` and each other `*.test.contract` beside it, `check`s the first screen and where each test ends (light, dark, two widths), relaunches once on real time, and reads those screens (on the web, also the ones the tests pass through) at the largest text size, where what spills is the app's layout to fix, with a remedy that keeps the text's size (no `line-clamp` in a list's row; `hyphens="auto"` only on a text of one word, which a UILabel breaks between syllables when it is longer than its line); `verify ios` also plays real touches on a long list on the first screen, once per build, and says `scrolling: like UIKit` or what a person would notice, each with UIKit's value and its cause, counting only what the app can fix: one report. A clean run on the app's platform is done.|
|`agent web --storage s1 "clock data" "tap add" "check both"`|Drives the app by hand, to see why something fails; `--keep-storage` reopens saved data.|
|`web`, `ios --run`, `windows --run`|For a person watching: its URL, rebuilds on save; a simulator; a window (from SSH, on the signed-in desktop).|
|`share`|For a person to try an iPhone app on their own phone: prints an AppDrop link that installs it. Run it when the app is ready for them, and again after each change they should see; send the link it prints.|

`verify`, `test` and `agent` compile, build and serve their own copy, saying a compile error as `contract build` does: no `contract build` before them, no dev server. `test linux` and `agent linux` do not build: run `bun exact.mjs linux` first and after each edit; nor do `test android` and `agent android`, which drive the APK `bun exact.mjs android` builds and installs on the device `ANDROID_SERIAL` names (`verify android` builds it). Run `verify` when the features work; `verify ios` or `verify android` once at the end for a phone app. On Windows, `test windows`,
`agent windows` and `verify windows` build first and drive headless at `app.json`'s `host.windows.window` size, in
DejaVu Sans with no frame; `verify windows` also captures the app as it opens on the desktop (`windows-window.png`):
judge the look from that one. Windows uses ink by default, or CPU when the manifest declares `game`; `host.windows.painter: "ink"` or `"cpu"` selects either painter. `EXACT_PAINTER` overrides either choice. Headless drives explicitly use CPU unless overridden ([painter choices](reference.md#windows-painter)). A screenshot path with a space is quoted: `"screenshot 'C:\a b\x.png'"`. A screen you
want checked or captured is a test's end; a drive takes any others (`resize`, `prefer …`, `screenshot`).
Create seam types once with `bun exact.mjs contract types app.contract -o app.contract.d.ts`.
`contract build` refreshes that declaration after a successful compile and reports
the change on stderr. `contract types --check app.contract` checks freshness without writing.
`bun exact.mjs update` reports lock drift after this checkout moves; `bun exact.mjs lock`
refreshes it. `contract migrate app.contract` rewrites retired Contract syntax;
[the Snapback upgrade note](../snapback4/README.md#updating-an-inherited-app) covers
mutation refusals too.
Keep scratch files in `.exact/` and helper scripts you commit (a screenshot comparer) in
`tools/`: neither makes the build stale. Other files you add may (a Python helper under
`scripts/`, a JSON file `app.ts` imports). Nothing the app reads belongs in `tools/`: an edit
there never counts as a change.

**To check a screen against a reference** (the original's screenshot, a design), drive to it and
take `"screenshot .exact/home.png compare ref/home.png"`: it says in text, node by node, where
the two differ, and draws `home.diff.png`, so neither picture needs viewing. On the web,
`agent web --url /item/7` opens at a page, and a capture of the whole page compares at its height.

`agent ios` is the app as a person sees it, UIKit's bars included, with screenshots a pixel a
point (`--scale 3`: the device's): no other simulator tool is needed ([ios-driving](recipes/ios-driving.md)).

- **Expressions** are TypeScript's: what compiles means what it means in TypeScript, and
  what does not is refused with what to write. The web's string and array methods are
  methods (`s.trim()`, `xs.filter(x => …)`, `xs.length`); the rest are functions
  (`first(xs)`, `round(n)`). What differs: no truthiness; absence is an option (`none`,
  `some(x)`, `match`), not `null`; a value never changes (`xs.concat([x])`, a record copy
  `Shape(old, field=value)`); `==` compares lists and records by value; a stored number is
  finite (a `NaN` refuses the commit). A presentation order by one key is
  `sortBy(xs, x => x.name)`, stable (`"desc"` third; a second key is an earlier `sortBy`), not
  `sort`; grouping, joining and a stored or locale order are the data module's, and the view
  names the order it relies on where it reads it (`resource tasks = loadTasksByDueDate()`).
  Nothing runs because a value changed: an event runs an action, which passes its captured
  arguments, then the payload (`toggle(i.id)` gets the bool). Its writes land when it ends, so a
  later line reads the old value: bind the new one (`let n = go(nav, url)`, `nav = n`, read `n`).
- **Data.** A `resource` is a reactive read (`pending(x)`, `failed(x)`); a `mutation` a
  write (`queue` keeps them in order, `refreshes` re-reads, `then` runs an action: clear
  the field only on an ok reply, as `afterAdd` does). Only the root declares them;
  children take `props`. For a mutation without `queue`, the action that sends it must
  not also assign its slot to `none`: assignments commit after sends and can discard its
  new reply. Hide an old error with `pending(added)`. `none` means the slot contains no
  reply, not failure; use `failure(added)` to show request failures and match the reply
  to handle a domain refusal.
- **Refreshes.** Include every resource the write changes (`refreshes groceries, counts`).

**The data module** answers each source with exactly its declared shape: an extra
field fails a resource or voids a mutation’s reply, whose slot keeps its old value.
Type the function returning a reply (`Promise<Result<'post'>>`) so the build names
an extra field. It reaches only what its `grants` name. A value fixed at build, such as an
API's origin, is `const API = import.meta.env.API_BASE_URL` at its top level, the name declared
in `app.json`'s `env` ([rest-backend](recipes/rest-backend.md)). A failed read should
fail its resource so Exact can retain its previous answer; a mutation may return
a shaped domain refusal for its action to handle
([fetch-loading-error](recipes/fetch-loading-error.md)). The clock and
randomness are refused there; time comes as an argument. A date from a value
works (`new Date(ms)`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`). `console.log` appears in the agent’s
`logs` and its last lines in a failed test’s notes. It imports its own `.ts`/`.js` and pure-JS npm
packages (ESM or CommonJS, a `browser` build first); one needing Node (`fs`, `Buffer`), the DOM or a native
addon is refused by name. Type an untyped one with `@types/<name>` or `declare module '<name>';` in a `.d.ts`.

```ts
import type { Answer, Result, Sources, Storage } from './app.contract.d.ts';

export const grants = 'fs.read app:/data/items.json\nfs.write app:/data/items.json';

type Item = Result<'loadItems'>[number];
const FILE = 'app:/data/items.json';
const load = (storage: Storage): Promise<Item[]> => storage.fs.readFile(FILE).then(
  (bytes) => JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes)),
  (e) => { if (e.code === 'ENOENT') return []; throw e; }); // no file yet ('bake', the build, passes)
const save = async (storage: Storage, items: Item[]) => {
  await storage.fs.atomicWriteFile(FILE, new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(items)));
  return { ok: true, error: '' };
};

const sources: Sources = {
  loadItems: (_args, _store, storage) => load(storage),
  addItem: async ([title], _store, storage) => {
    const all = await load(storage), same = all.find((i) => i.title.toLowerCase() === title.toLowerCase());
    if (same) return { ok: false, error: `${same.title} is already on the list.` }; // a refusal is a reply too
    return save(storage, [...all, { id: String(all.length + 1), title, done: false }]);
  },
  setDone: async ([id, done], _store, storage) => save(storage, (await load(storage)).map((i) => (i.id === id ? { ...i, done } : i))),
};
export const answer: Answer = (source, args, store, storage, native) => sources[source](args, store, storage, native);
```

**The tests** drive by `testId` on every host, each from empty storage:

```contract-test
test "an item is added, a repeat refused, checked off and kept"
  type "draft" "Milk"
  tap "add"
  clock data
  expect text "left" == "1 item left"
  type "draft" "milk"
  tap "add"
  clock data
  expect text "add-error" == "Milk is already on the list."
  expect text "draft" == "milk"
  tap "done-1"
  clock data
  reload
  expect state groceries.0 .done == true
  expect text "left" == "0 items left"
```

Every step, launch line and `verify` flag is on the card.

Interactive web drives also accept `reload` (keeps storage and fetch faults) and
`pick <input-id> <path>`. `agent web --help all` lists driver capabilities.

Each mutation source request adds one millisecond of UI virtual time after the
step, including timer mutations issued during that advance. Reads and
continuations add none; arguments within an atomic action keep its clock
snapshot. The backend’s clock stays its own.

| To assert | Write | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A node is there, or not | `expect tree has "<testId>"`, `expect tree missing "<testId>"` | `lacks`, `contains`, `not has`. It matches a `testId` only, never a label or text, unlike `tap` |
| A node's text | `expect text "<testId>" == "the whole text"` | `contains`, `!=`. The text is compared whole, and a node with no text of its own reads its descendants' joined: a row's testId reads its buttons' labels too, so put the testId on the text node |
| State | `expect state lib.notes.0.title == "Milk"` (two list indexes in a row take a space: `grid.0 .1`; a drive's `clock until state` takes the same path), `== []`, `== none`, `== true` | an expression on the right |
| A failed resource or mutation request | `expect text` on the view's `match failure(x) { case some(f) => f.code, case none => "" }`; `failed(x)` accepts either slot | `failure(x).code` without extracting the option. A thrown refusal is a request failure; an authored `{ok: false}` is a normal result |

## Pitfalls that cost the most

1. **Styling a platform control.** Paint (`background-color`, `border`, `font-size`)
   on a `button`, field or bar makes it your box. Emphasis is a part (above) or
   `buttonStyle="filled"` on the screen's main action. A `button` with no
   `buttonStyle` is the platform's: tinted text on iOS, so one that must read as a
   button there says `"bordered"`, and Cancel or Edit says nothing. A field on its own is
   the platform's bordered one; a document's own text (a note's title and body, as Notes
   draws them) says `border="none"`, and a chat's composer is `chat-thread`'s.
2. **A `header` holds a heading (`h1 "Title"`), one text after it (the subtitle) and
   buttons** (or a search field, a `tablist`); anything else isn't in the iOS bar. A
   control fixed under the bar goes with an inline title (`h2`); one that may scroll
   away, in the list's first section.
3. **`width="100%"` with padding overflows**, as in CSS: drop the width; a `flex=1` field
   takes `min-width=0`.

Consecutive `match` blocks in an action all run in order. Nest a match in the
selected arm, or use `if`/`else`, for exclusive paths. Action reads still see
the state from the action’s start.

how (snippets compile)
a second screen, a sheet: A screen is a route, not an `if`; a sheet's root adds `navigationPresentation="modal"`, its Cancel the `id` `navigationBack` names (`pattern list-detail`).
  routes nav
    home "/"
      edit "/edit"
  action open
    nav = push(nav, "/edit")
  action back
    nav = back(nav)
  action save
    nav = back(nav)
  main navigationKey=`${top(nav).id}` navigationBack="back"
    for e in stack(nav) key=e.id
      if e.name == "home"
        column navigationKey=`${e.id}` position="absolute" inset=0
          header
            text "Notes" role="heading" aria-level=1
            button press=open
              text "New"
      if e.name == "edit"
        column navigationKey=`${e.id}` navigationPresentation="modal" position="absolute" inset=0
          header
            button id="back" press=back aria-label="Cancel"
              image "symbol:close"
            text "New" role="heading"
            button press=save buttonStyle="bordered-prominent" aria-label="Save"
              image "symbol:checkmark"
a confirmation: What can't be undone (Delete) asks first. `aria-label` is the question; actions run their `press` and close (`command="close"`); Cancel has no `press`. Open it with `command="show-modal"` or `showModal(id)`.
  state n = 1
  action remove
    n = 0
  button commandfor="remove" command="show-modal"
    text "Remove"
  dialog id="remove" role="alertdialog" aria-label="Delete it?"
    button press=remove destructive=true commandfor="remove" command="close"
      text "Delete"
    button commandfor="remove" command="close"
      text "Cancel"
a timer: `every(ms, action)` repeats; `after(ms, action)` runs once. Options: `wait=frame|update|scrollend|idle`, `max=ms`, `tolerance=ms`. See `contract vocab timers`.
  state now = 0
  task tick mount
    every(1000, step)
  action step
    now = performanceNow()
  text `${now}`
keeping a value: Root `state` only: a number, string or bool (or an option or list of one) up to 16 KB. Records belong in a source (`files-and-grants`).
  state units = "C" persist
colour: Leave the accent unsaid (a brand is an app.tamber) and controls unpainted; elsewhere a role (follows the scheme): text `label`, `secondary-label`; a card `secondary-background`; a fill `secondary-fill`; a hue `system-red`…. No hex.
  main
    text "Total" color="-exact-secondary-label"
    view padding=12 background-color="-exact-secondary-background"
      text "Over" color="-exact-system-red"
reading and writing data: `loadItems` and `addItem` are in app.ts and answer exactly their shape; a refusal is a reply (`ok: false, error`), not a throw. `then act` after `refreshes` clears the field on an ok reply; `pending(added)` stops a second send.
  shape Reply
    ok: bool
  resource items = loadItems() as shape string[] else empty()
  mutation added as shape Reply refreshes items
  action add
    send added = addItem("Milk")
  text items.join(", ")
a dated record: The write reads the clock, not a ticked `now`, and stores `at`; `performanceNow()` alone is 0 each launch. `"iso"` is the day, compared as text; its label `formatDay(at, now, …)`: Today, Yesterday. Tests pin `epoch` and `time-zone`.
  shape Time
    epochAtZero: number
    utcOffset: number
  state days = []
  resource time = exactTime() as shape Time
  action log
    let at = time.epochAtZero + performanceNow()
    days = days.concat([formatDate(at, time.utcOffset, "iso")])

app.ts
// Starter: two tabs, each its own stack: a list that pushes a detail in each.
// The root tablist is the iOS tab bar; a screen a tab pushed survives a visit to the other.
// Each tab's list has the bar's search field, its own query (`contract vocab search`).
use EmptyState from "exact:content"

routes nav
  tab places "/"
    place "/place/:id"
  tab saved "/saved"
    savedPlace "/saved/:id"

shape Place
  id: string
  name: string
  area: string
  about: string

fn nameOf(places: Place[], id: string): string = match first(places.filter(p => p.id == id)) { case some(p) => p.name, case none => "" }
fn matches(p: Place, q: string): bool = p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q.trim().toLowerCase()) or p.area.toLowerCase().includes(q.trim().toLowerCase())

component App
  state saved = [] persist
  state placesQuery = ""
  state savedQuery = ""
  resource places = loadPlaces() as shape Place[] else empty()
  derive placesShown = places.filter(p => matches(p, placesQuery))
  derive savedShown = places.filter(p => saved.includes(p.id) and matches(p, savedQuery))
  action pick(name: string)
    nav = select(nav, name)
  // A row is a link to its place; the browser's Back, Forward and a deep link arrive here too.
  action follow(url: string)
    nav = go(nav, url)
  action search(tab: string, v: string)
    if tab == "saved"
      savedQuery = v
    else
      placesQuery = v
  action toggle(id: string)
    saved = saved.includes(id) ? saved.filter(s => s != id) : saved.concat([id])
  view
    main navigationKey=`${top(nav).id}` navigationBack="back" navigate=follow testId="app" width="100%" height="100%"
      display="flex" flex-direction="column"
      column flex=1 min-height=0 position="relative"
        for t in nav.tabs key=t.name
          column role="tabpanel" id=`panel-${t.name}` position="absolute" inset=0
            for e in t.stack key=e.id
              column navigationKey=`${e.id}` navigationScroll=`content-${e.id}` position="absolute" inset=0
                display="flex" flex-direction="column"
                header display="flex" flex-wrap="wrap" align-items="center" gap=8 padding="8px 16px"
                  text (e.name == "places" ? "Starter" : e.name == "saved" ? "Saved" : nameOf(places, e.params.id))
                    role="heading" aria-level=(e.name == "places" or e.name == "saved" ? 1 : 2) flex=1
                  if e.name == "place" or e.name == "savedPlace"
                    button press=toggle(e.params.id) aria-label=(saved.includes(e.params.id) ? "Remove from Saved" : "Save")
                      testId=`save-${t.name}`
                      image (saved.includes(e.params.id) ? "symbol:bookmark-fill" : "symbol:bookmark")
                  if e.name == "places" or (e.name == "saved" and saved.length > 0)
                    input type="search" value=(t.name == "saved" ? savedQuery : placesQuery) input=search(t.name)
                      placeholder="Search" aria-label=(t.name == "saved" ? "Search Saved" : "Search Places")
                      testId=`search-${t.name}` width="100%"
                // An empty tab and a search with no match are each an `EmptyState` in the list's place.
                if e.name == "saved" and saved.length == 0
                  EmptyState(symbol="symbol:bookmark", title="No Saved Places", message="Open a place and tap the bookmark.")
                else if e.name == "places" or e.name == "saved"
                  if (t.name == "saved" ? savedShown : placesShown).length == 0 and not pending(places)
                    EmptyState(symbol="symbol:search", title="No Results", message="Check the spelling or try a new search.")
                  else
                    list id=`content-${e.id}` appearance="auto" listStyle="inset-grouped" flex=1 min-height=0
                      section
                        for p in (t.name == "saved" ? savedShown : placesShown) key=p.id
                          link href=(e.name == "saved" ? path("savedPlace", p.id) : path("place", p.id)) testId=`${t.name}-${p.id}`
                            column flex=1 min-width=0 gap=2 padding-top=4 padding-bottom=4
                              text p.name
                              text p.area font="-exact-subheadline" color="-exact-secondary-label"
                            image "symbol:forward-chevron"
                else
                  list id=`content-${e.id}` appearance="auto" listStyle="inset-grouped" flex=1 min-height=0
                    for p in places.filter(x => x.id == e.params.id) key=p.id
                      section
                        row
                          text "Area"
                          text p.area
                      section
                        row padding-top=10 padding-bottom=10
                          text p.about flex=1 min-width=0 testId=`about-${t.name}`
      row role="tablist" testId="tabs"
        button role="tab" aria-controls="panel-places" aria-selected=(nav.tab == "places") press=pick("places")
          testId="tab-places" flex=1
          image "symbol:home"
          text "Places"
        button role="tab" aria-controls="panel-saved" aria-selected=(nav.tab == "saved") press=pick("saved")
          testId="tab-saved" flex=1
          image "symbol:bookmark"
          text "Saved"
# Recipe: tabs

Use tabs for at least two top-level sections, each with its own route stack. A one-tab bar is a tell.

```contract
routes nav
  tab today "/"
  tab history "/history"
    day "/day/:key"

component App
  action pick(name: string)
    nav = select(nav, name)
  action follow(url: string)
    nav = go(nav, url)
  view
    main navigationKey=`${top(nav).id}` navigationBack="back" navigate=follow
      width="100%" height="100%" display="flex" flex-direction="column"
      column flex=1 min-height=0 position="relative"
        for t in nav.tabs key=t.name
          column role="tabpanel" id=`panel-${t.name}` position="absolute" inset=0
            for e in t.stack key=e.id
              column navigationKey=`${e.id}` navigationScroll=`content-${e.id}` position="absolute" inset=0
                header padding="8px 16px"
                  text (e.name == "today" ? "Today" : e.name == "history" ? "History" : e.params.key)
                    role="heading" aria-level=(e.name == "day" ? 2 : 1)
                scroll id=`content-${e.id}` flex=1 min-height=0
                  if e.name == "history"
                    link href=path("day", "2026-10-09") testId="day-2026-10-09"
                      text "Yesterday"
                  else
                    text "Nothing logged yet." color="-exact-secondary-label" padding=16
      row role="tablist"
        button role="tab" aria-controls="panel-today" aria-selected=(nav.tab == "today") press=pick("today")
          testId="tab-today" flex=1
          image "symbol:calendar"
          text "Today"
        button role="tab" aria-controls="panel-history" aria-selected=(nav.tab == "history") press=pick("history")
          testId="tab-history" flex=1
          image "symbol:chart"
          text "History"
```

```contract-test
test "each tab keeps its own stack"
  tap "tab-history"
  tap "day-2026-10-09"
  clock settle
  expect state nav.tab == "history"
  tap "tab-today"
  tap "tab-history"

# Recipe: porting an app, a release build, splitting the work

**Name the port when you make it:** `exact new <path> --name "Euxy" --bundle-id com.yourcompany.euxy`,
with the original's name and bundle id if it replaces the original on a device. A bundle id
changed after the first build makes the next build cold and leaves the app installed under the
old id, to delete by hand. Changing one later means app.json's `app.id`
(and an `appId` app.ts exports, which must agree). An app ships the platforms app.json names: a native verb names
its own on its first run, and `bun exact.mjs update --without <platform>` stops shipping one
(LLP 1153 D1). A port that ran `linux` once hears each `symbol:sf/…` warn that Linux draws it
blank until `update --without linux`; one that ran `mac` hears `tamber-unreachable` name a Mac
control that ignores the design (NSSlider's accent) until `update --without macos`. The SF
Symbols the web draws blank are one warning line.

**Comparing a port with the original.** `agent ios --touch platform` makes each tap a real touch,
which opens UIKit's menus and reaches a native module's own controls: drive with it to compare a
port's screens with the original's ([ios-driving](ios-driving.md)). Porting a React Native app,
read [its pitfalls](../agent-pitfalls.md#porting-a-react-native-app) first.

**What ships.** `ios --release` builds what ships; it ignores `EXACT_AGENT`, so drive the
development build. A first takes two minutes: start it early, `--prebuild --release`; later
`ios --release` waits for a build still running, then takes seconds.
A `--touch platform` drive turns the simulator's accessibility on while it runs (an app launched
with it on loads UIKit's accessibility runtime: 1.4 s) and restores what it found at its end. A
launch that slow (`main→didFinishLaunching` over a second) had it on before; this turns it off,
with no reboot:

```sh
for k in AutomationEnabled AccessibilityEnabled ApplicationAccessibilityEnabled; do xcrun simctl spawn <udid> defaults delete com.apple.Accessibility $k; done
```

A launch times the installed build, never a plan an `agent ios` drive swapped in: `bun exact.mjs
ios` each variant first. `SIMCTL_CHILD_EXACT_SMOKE=1 xcrun simctl launch --console-pty <udid>
<bundle id>` prints Exact's phases to first draw (exec→main, scene, runner and layout, apply,
painted) and exits; a data module's first answer is a hook's to stamp.

**Sound, MIDI and a transport are Exact's** (`sequence`, `play(tracks…)`, `exactMIDI()`,
`sendMIDI`, `midimessage`: [the guide's "Sound, MIDI and media"](../contract-for-agents.md#sound-midi-and-media),
`apps/metronome`). A [native module](native-module.md) is for what Exact lacks; never port an
audio or MIDI engine into one.

**Splitting a port among helpers:** commit the seam between the halves first (the shared types,
the native module's interface), then start each helper in the background from that commit,
owning its half and stubbing none of another's. Keep test screens off branches you merge, and
keep working while they run.
# Recipe: your own REST server

The REST starter creates a shared-list app and a Bun server:

```sh
bun exact.mjs pattern rest
```

The [REST starter](../patterns/rest/app.contract) writes the Contract app and
Bun server together. Its data source validates read responses before returning
them. When a read fails because of a transport error, an HTTP error or an invalid
response, Exact keeps the prior answer and exposes the failure. The view shows
that answer only when `lib.owner == persona`; otherwise, it shows loading or
retry state. A validated empty list is a successful answer.

The starter's writes return shaped replies for operation refusals, such as a
duplicate title, so `then` can keep the form open and display the reason. Its
mutation helper also converts transport failures to shaped replies. If a source
lets a transport rejection escape instead, the mutation gets no new reply, keeps
its previous value, and does not run `then`; `failure(mutation)` explains the
request failure.

The sample `persona` values are public development identities. A real app should
put a stable, non-secret principal id in the resource call and keep bearer
credentials in the granted store. It should await an app-owned current-session
helper inside the data source before issuing authenticated requests, then verify
that the session authorizes the principal named by the resource. Exact does not
provide that session helper. This starter demonstrates owner gating, not a full
authentication lifecycle; a real authenticated view must also gate retained
answers by the app-owned authorized principal and auth generation.

## Where the server lives

`test`, `verify` and `agent --test` start the server themselves on an empty database
and stop it after; start none of your own for them. They find it this way:

- **Its entry:** `server.ts`, `server/index.ts` or `server/server.ts`, or the one `app.json` names:
  `"commands": { "server": ["bun", "server/main.ts"] }`.
  Arguments after the entry in `commands.server` are passed through in order.
- **Its address:** the first `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` in `app.ts` as the build has it, a setting's
  value in place of its read (or in a module it imports, as the starter's `API`). To use another port, change it there; the server reads it from the same constant.
  An origin fixed at build (a deployed API's) is a setting: `"env": ["API_BASE_URL"]` in `app.json`,
  `const API = import.meta.env.API_BASE_URL ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:8080'` in `app.ts`, its value from the
  environment, `.env.local` or `.env`, in that order. Keep the local server's address as the default.
  The value is inlined into the module on every host, so a secret does not belong there.
- **Its database:** the path in `DB`, which the entry or a module it imports reads:
  `new Database(process.env.DB ?? 'data.db')`.
  If the server keeps no database, set `"server": { "database": false }` beside
  `commands` to omit `DB` and skip scratch database creation and removal; otherwise
  an entry that does not read `DB` is refused.

A dev server already on that port makes them stop and name its pid: stop it first.
# Recipe: fetch with loading, error and retry

```contract
shape Feed
  owner: string
  posts: string[]

component App
  state account = "default"
  resource feed = loadFeed(account) as shape Feed else empty()
  action reload
    refresh feed
  view
    column
      button press=reload testId="refresh"
        text "Refresh"
      scroll refresh=reload refreshing=(pending(feed) and feed.owner == account) flex=1 min-height=0
        if pending(feed)
          progress aria-label="Loading" testId="loading"
        if failed(feed)
          text "Couldn't load the feed." testId="error"
          button press=reload testId="retry"
            text "Try Again"
        if feed.owner == account
          if feed.posts.length == 0 and not failed(feed)
            text "No posts yet."
          for p, i in feed.posts key=p
            text p testId=`post-${i}`
```

`empty()` sets `owner` to `""`; account IDs must be nonempty. The owner check
hides A's retained rows after switching to B, even if B fails. A failed refresh
of A keeps its rows beside Retry; a valid empty answer replaces them.
Use the same check for a server or workspace: its answer names that owner.

```ts
import type { Answer, Result } from './app.contract.d.ts';

const API = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com';
export const grants = `net.fetch ${API}`;

function isPost(p: unknown): p is { title: string } {
  return p !== null && typeof p === 'object' && 'title' in p && typeof p.title === 'string';
}

export const answer: Answer = async (_source, [owner]): Promise<Result<'loadFeed'>> => {
  const response = await fetch(`${API}/posts?_limit=10`, { exactTimeout: 10000 });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error('The feed request failed.');
  }
  const body: unknown = await response.json();
  if (!Array.isArray(body) || !body.every(isPost)) {
    throw new Error('The feed response is invalid.');
  }
  return { owner, posts: body.map((p): string => p.title) };
};
```

```contract-test
test "a failed refresh retains rows and retries"
  clock data
  fail fetch "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com"
  tap "refresh"
  expect tree has "loading"
  expect tree has "post-0"
  clock data
  expect tree has "post-0"
  expect tree has "error"
  pass fetch "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com"
  tap "retry"
  clock data
  expect tree missing "error"
```

`fail fetch` rejects; it cannot delay or supply an HTTP status/body. Use a
[test server](rest-backend.md) for those.

For private data, also gate by the authorized principal and auth generation:
A → B → A must reject the first A session's answers. Check it before writing a cache
after an await. Await session prerequisites in the source; dependencies do not
sequence requests. See the
[data guide](../contract-for-agents.md#data-requests-and-side-effects).

Development `state.resourceStatus` reports retained answers and argument equality; `failed` and `failures` give the error and count. It changes neither
retention nor authorization. `with` only admits persisted answers at boot.

content.content:
# Recipe: a native module in Swift

**Sound and MIDI are built in** ([guide](../contract-for-agents.md#sound-midi-and-media),
`apps/metronome`): write no module. Another platform API with no view (a hook) is the module `app.ts` asks: `modules/apple/*.swift`, one `ExactModule` subclass that `let exactModule` names.
app.json needs nothing for it ([app-json](app-json.md)).

```swift
import Foundation

final class Engine: ExactModule {
    override func call(_ request: [String: Any]) throws -> [String: Any] {
        switch request["op"] as? String {
        case "flags": return ["autoPlay": UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: "AutoPlay")]
        default: throw ExactNativeRefusal("engine answers flags")
        }
    }
    override func later(_ request: [String: Any], reply: ExactReply) {
        DispatchQueue.global().async { reply.send(["ok": true]) }
    }
}
let exactModule: ExactModule.Type = Engine.self
```

```contract
shape Flags
  autoPlay: bool

shape Reply
  ok: bool

component App
  resource flags = engineFlags() as shape Flags else empty()
  mutation played as shape Reply
  action play
    send played = enginePlay()
  view
    button press=play testId="play"
      text (flags.autoPlay ? "Playing" : "Play")
```

```ts
import type { Answer, Result, Sources } from './app.contract.d.ts';

const sources: Sources = {
  engineFlags: async (_args, _store, _storage, native) => {
    if (!native?.available) return { autoPlay: false }; // the build, or no module here
    native.watch('flags');
    try { return native.call({ op: 'flags' }) as Result<'engineFlags'>; }
    catch { return (await native.later({ op: 'flags' })) as Result<'engineFlags'>; } // the web
  },
  enginePlay: async (_args, _store, _storage, native) =>
    (await native!.later({ op: 'play' })) as Result<'enginePlay'>,
};
export const answer: Answer = (source, args, store, storage, native) =>
  sources[source](args, store, storage, native);
```

- **`call`** runs on main within the answer's 100 ms; throw to refuse. **`later`** replies once,

# Vendored Ibex split crates — Exact integration ledger

## Windows WebSocket readiness

`crates/ibex2/src/transport/websocket.rs` subscribes to writable readiness only
while output is pending. Windows rearms readiness after a blocked read; keeping
writable interest on an empty output queue makes an outstanding receive spin.
The idle-receive regression in `websocket_tests.rs` checks that the pump stays
parked and still wakes on cancellation.

## Mac widget Keychain (LLP 1126.001 WP16)

`crates/ibex2/src/secrets/darwin_keychain.mm` selects the restricted
`ExactKeychainAccessGroup` in the data-protection Keychain for a provisioned
Apple widget cohort. Ordinary Mac apps keep the login Keychain. The containing
app migrates its service's login items on its first provisioned launch;
copy failure keeps the old item, and an existing shared item wins. Migration
runs once per process, from `prepare` only. An unreadable item is skipped;
errors are logged without withholding the app's I/O. Retained items can be
retried on the next launch. The move is one-way. Extensions never migrate.
The Objective-C fixture in
`host/apple/tests/fixtures/keychain-migration.mm` exercises retries and failures
with substituted Security calls; signed Keychain access still needs profiles.

## Snapshot and update recipe

- Upstream: `https://github.com/expo/ibex.git` at
  `a0183568e8229b8243629cdb26cd4a88ac4e2abd` (2026-10-30).
- Source trees: `crates/{ibex2,ibex2-sqlite,hermes-lean-sys,hermes-lean-sys-installer}`.
- Data inputs: `scripts/icu74-filter-{root-en,en-intl}.json` and
  `third_party/wpt/urltestdata.json`.
- Hermes bundle is `hermes-vanilla-d412d3bd8512-v5`, source
  `d412d3bd…` / Hermes `260318099.0.4`. Repository engine-output directories
  remain absent; builds validate the paired compiler and VM in the bundle cache.
- The two standalone `Cargo.lock` files under `ibex2` and
  `hermes-lean-sys-installer` are consumer integration files. The installer
  shares pinned dependency versions with Exact's root lock.

## Rust data sources

A data crate answers the view's sources in Rust instead of `app.ts`: an app's
`data/` crate ([Caltrain](../apps/caltrain/data/src/lib.rs),
[Fieldnotes](../apps/fieldnotes/data/src/lib.rs)) or a game's `game.data`
(`game/README.md`). Its type implements `exact_runner::DataSource`:

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `query(source, args)` | Answer now, with no I/O: the build bakes this into the plan for the first frame. `Err(DataError::Unavailable(…))` leaves the resource unbaked; every host asks again at launch. |
| `answer(store, source, args)` | At run time: `Answer::Now(value)`, or `Answer::Later(request)` for the host to run (storage, `fetch`). The default is `query`. |
| `parse(store, source, args, outcome)` | What the host brought back for that request: answer, or hand back one more request. |
| `app_id()` | The app's identity, which names its storage: `com.example.my-app-3f9a2c` (`exact new` writes the name and six random hex digits), or for a game `com.exact.<Game::ID>` unless its app.json names one. A source with no id has no app storage on Apple and Linux. |
| `grants()` | One grant per line, the lines `app.ts`'s `grants` takes (`net.fetch …`, `sqlite.open …`, `fs.read …`). |

A record is positional: `Value::record(vec![…])` takes its fields in the order
the shape declares them. `bun exact.mjs contract rust app.contract -o
/tmp/shapes.rs` writes each shape as a struct with its fields in that order;
`Value::Number`, `Value::str`, `Value::Bool` and `Value::list` are the rest.

### Where data lives: app storage, not secrets

Keep app and game data (best times, settings, saves, notes) in **app
storage**: SQLite databases and files under `app:/data`, the storage `app.ts`
reaches as `storage.sqlite` and `storage.fs`. A Rust source asks for it with
`exact_data::storage::request(op, args)` as an `Answer::Later`, and reads the
reply in `parse` with `exact_data::storage::response(outcome)`, which is the
JSON result or the host's message. The operations:

| `op` | `args` | Reply |
|---|---|---|
| `"sqlite"` | `{"path": "app:/data/x.db", "commands": [{"kind": "execute" or "query", "sql", "params"}]}` | One result per command, in order: a query's `{"columns", "rows"}` (an integer is `{"integer": "7"}`, text a string), an execute's `{"changes", "lastInsertRowid"}` |
| `"sqlite.transaction"` | the same, `execute` commands only | the executes' results, all or none |
| `"fs.readFile"`, `"fs.atomicWriteFile"`, `"fs.writeFile"`, `"fs.appendFile"` | `{"path"}`, and `"text"` (or `"bytes"`) to write | read: `{"base64"}`; write: `null` |
| `"fs.mkdir"`, `"fs.rm"`, `"fs.stat"`, `"fs.readdir"`, `"fs.rename"`, `"fs.copyFile"` | `{"path"}`, and `"destination"` to move or copy | as `storage.fs` answers |
| `"fs.compressImage"` | `{"path", "destination", "maxDimension", "maxBytes"}`, and `"type"` (`"image/png"`; absent or `null` is JPEG), `"rotate"`, `"flip"`, `"crop"` | `{"path", "type", "size", "width", "height"}`, as `storage.fs.compressImage` answers |
| `"fs.transformImage"` | `{"path", "destination"}` and `storage.fs.transformImage`'s options beside them (`"rotate"`, `"crop"`, `"metadata"`, …; `null` is absent) | `{"path", "type", "size", "width", "height", "colorSpace", "hdr", "metadata"}`, as it answers |

Grant what it touches: `sqlite.open app:/data/x.db`, `fs.read app:/data`,
`fs.write app:/data`. Storage is asynchronous and starts after first pixel. It
is absent at build, so `query` answers a placeholder, and in a scripted drive
that names no scratch store: there `response` is an error, and the source
answers as if nothing were kept. `--storage <name>` gives a drive a store kept
between native drives (`--reset-storage` empties it); on the web the next drive
keeps it with `--keep-storage`. An authored test gets an empty one, and its `reload` restarts
on it. A game's data crate takes these crates from the SDK
(`exact-data.workspace = true`, `serde_json.workspace = true`).

Best times, one row a level, decided in SQL. This is the platformer's source
(the diary's R6). One request reads the previous best and writes the run where
it beats it:

```rust
use exact_data::storage;
use exact_runner::{Answer, DataError, DataSource, Outcome, Store, Value};
use serde_json::json;

const DB: &str = "app:/data/scores.db";
const TABLE: &str = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS best (level INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ms INTEGER NOT NULL)";

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Scores;

impl DataSource for Scores {
    fn app_id(&self) -> &str { "com.exact.hopper" }
    fn grants(&self) -> &str { "sqlite.open app:/data/scores.db" }
    fn query(&mut self, source: &str, _: &[Value]) -> Result<Value, DataError> {
        match source {
            "best" => Ok(Value::record(vec![Value::list(vec![])])), // the build's first frame: nothing kept
            _ => Err(DataError::Unavailable("asked at run time".into())),
        }
    }
    fn answer(&mut self, _: &mut Store, source: &str, args: &[Value]) -> Result<Answer, DataError> {
        let commands = match (source, args) {
            ("best", _) => json!([{"kind": "execute", "sql": TABLE, "params": []},
                {"kind": "query", "sql": "SELECT level, ms FROM best ORDER BY level", "params": []}]),
            ("finish", [Value::Number(level), Value::Number(ms)]) => json!([{"kind": "execute", "sql": TABLE, "params": []},
                {"kind": "execute", "sql": "INSERT INTO best VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT(level) DO UPDATE SET ms = excluded.ms WHERE excluded.ms < best.ms", "params": [level, ms]}]),
            _ => return Err(DataError::UnknownSource(source.into())),
        };
        Ok(Answer::Later(storage::request("sqlite", json!({"path": DB, "commands": commands}))))
    }
    fn parse(&mut self, _: &mut Store, source: &str, _: &[Value], outcome: Outcome) -> Result<Answer, DataError> {
        let results = storage::response(outcome);
        let int = |cell: &serde_json::Value| cell["integer"].as_str().and_then(|n| n.parse::<f64>().ok());
        Ok(Answer::Now(match source {
            // No storage here (a drive with no scratch store): nothing kept.
            "best" => Value::record(vec![Value::list(results.ok().and_then(|r| r[1]["rows"].as_array().cloned()).unwrap_or_default()
                .iter().filter_map(|row| Some(Value::record(vec![Value::Number(int(&row[0])?), Value::Number(int(&row[1])?)]))).collect())]),
            _ => Value::record(vec![Value::Bool(results.map_err(DataError::Unavailable)?[1]["changes"].as_str() == Some("1"))]), // a new best?
        }))
    }
}
```

`Store` (`store.get`, `store.set`, under `secret.keep <name>`) is for
**secrets**: a session token, a key. Apple keeps them in the Keychain, Linux
in a file per secret only the user can read (`0600`, under
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/exact/<app id>/secrets`; not encrypted), and the web in
`localStorage`; Windows keeps them in memory for now. The host reads them into a snapshot before boot, so a
read is synchronous, and a scripted drive never keeps them. A best time is not
a secret: keep it in app storage.

between native drives (`--reset-storage` empties it); on the web the next drive
keeps it with `--keep-storage`. An authored test gets an empty one, and its `reload` restarts
on it. A game's data crate takes these crates from the SDK
(`exact-data.workspace = true`, `serde_json.workspace = true`).

Best times, one row a level, decided in SQL. This is the platformer's source
(the diary's R6). One request reads the previous best and writes the run where
it beats it:

```rust
use exact_data::storage;
use exact_runner::{Answer, DataError, DataSource, Outcome, Store, Value};
use serde_json::json;

const DB: &str = "app:/data/scores.db";
const TABLE: &str = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS best (level INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ms INTEGER NOT NULL)";

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Scores;

impl DataSource for Scores {
    fn app_id(&self) -> &str { "com.exact.hopper" }
    fn grants(&self) -> &str { "sqlite.open app:/data/scores.db" }
    fn query(&mut self, source: &str, _: &[Value]) -> Result<Value, DataError> {
        match source {
            "best" => Ok(Value::record(vec![Value::list(vec![])])), // the build's first frame: nothing kept
            _ => Err(DataError::Unavailable("asked at run time".into())),
        }
    }
    fn answer(&mut self, _: &mut Store, source: &str, args: &[Value]) -> Result<Answer, DataError> {
        let commands = match (source, args) {
            ("best", _) => json!([{"kind": "execute", "sql": TABLE, "params": []},
                {"kind": "query", "sql": "SELECT level, ms FROM best ORDER BY level", "params": []}]),
            ("finish", [Value::Number(level), Value::Number(ms)]) => json!([{"kind": "execute", "sql": TABLE, "params": []},
                {"kind": "execute", "sql": "INSERT INTO best VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT(level) DO UPDATE SET ms = excluded.ms WHERE excluded.ms < best.ms", "params": [level, ms]}]),
            _ => return Err(DataError::UnknownSource(source.into())),
        };
        Ok(Answer::Later(storage::request("sqlite", json!({"path": DB, "commands": commands}))))
    }
    fn parse(&mut self, _: &mut Store, source: &str, _: &[Value], outcome: Outcome) -> Result<Answer, DataError> {
        let results = storage::response(outcome);
        let int = |cell: &serde_json::Value| cell["integer"].as_str().and_then(|n| n.parse::<f64>().ok());
        Ok(Answer::Now(match source {
            // No storage here (a drive with no scratch store): nothing kept.
            "best" => Value::record(vec![Value::list(results.ok().and_then(|r| r[1]["rows"].as_array().cloned()).unwrap_or_default()
                .iter().filter_map(|row| Some(Value::record(vec![Value::Number(int(&row[0])?), Value::Number(int(&row[1])?)]))).collect())]),
            _ => Value::record(vec![Value::Bool(results.map_err(DataError::Unavailable)?[1]["changes"].as_str() == Some("1"))]), // a new best?
        }))
    }
}
```

`Store` (`store.get`, `store.set`, under `secret.keep <name>`) is for
**secrets**: a session token, a key. Apple keeps them in the Keychain, Linux
in a file per secret only the user can read (`0600`, under
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/exact/<app id>/secrets`; not encrypted), and the web in
`localStorage`; Windows keeps them in memory for now. The host reads them into a snapshot before boot, so a
read is synchronous, and a scripted drive never keeps them. A best time is not
a secret: keep it in app storage.

platform=iphonesimulator; target_arches='arm64;x86_64'; deployment_target=15.0; profile=min-size-release ;;
  aarch64-apple-tvos)
    [[ "$host_os" == Darwin ]] || { echo "$target requires a macOS host" >&2; exit 2; }
    platform=appletvos; target_arches=arm64; deployment_target=15.0; profile=min-size-release ;;
  aarch64-apple-tvos-simulator)
    [[ "$host_os" == Darwin ]] || { echo "$target requires a macOS host" >&2; exit 2; }
    platform=appletvsimulator; target_arches=arm64; deployment_target=15.0; profile=min-size-release ;;
  x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
    [[ "$host_os" == Linux && "$host_arch" == x86_64 ]] \
      || { echo "$target requires an x86_64 Linux host" >&2; exit 2; } ;;
  aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu)
    [[ "$host_os" == Linux && "$host_arch" == arm64 ]] \
      || { echo "$target requires an arm64 Linux host" >&2; exit 2; } ;;
  aarch64-linux-android)
    # Cross-built with the NDK from a macOS or Linux host. Hermes's own
    # HERMES_IS_ANDROID build needs fbjni and a JVM for Unicode and Intl; a
    # native embedder has neither, so this bundle takes Unicode from a static
    # ICU (as the Linux bundles do) and has no Intl.
    android_ndk="${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:-}"
    if [[ -z "$android_ndk" ]]; then
      sdk="${ANDROID_HOME:-${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT:-$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}}"
      android_ndk="$(ls -d "$sdk"/ndk/* 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort -V | tail -1)"
    fi
    [[ -f "$android_ndk/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake" ]] \
      || { echo "$target needs an Android NDK (set ANDROID_NDK_HOME)" >&2; exit 2; }
    android_api="${IBEX_ANDROID_API:-30}"
    profile=min-size-release ;;
  *) usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

for command_name in cmake git node python3; do
  command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "$command_name is required" >&2; exit 1; }
done
if [[ "$host_os" == Darwin ]]; then
  for command_name in lipo libtool xcodebuild; do
    command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
      || { echo "$command_name is required" >&2; exit 1; }
  done
else
  for command_name in make ninja nm pkg-config; do
    command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
      || { echo "$command_name is required" >&2; exit 1; }
  done
fi

cache_root="${IBEX_HERMES_RELEASE_CACHE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/ibex/hermes-vanilla-release}"
cache_dir="$cache_root/$commit/$target"
source_dir="$cache_root/upstream"
icu_source_dir="$cache_root/icu-upstream"
build_dir="$cache_dir/build"
