A list row's `delete=action` is its swipe to delete, UIKit's on iOS (`contract vocab swipe`). Other swipe actions are a hand-written swipe row, a `scroll` laid out as a row (`display="flex"`) whose content iOS needs exactly the scroll's size ([pitfalls](agent-pitfalls.md), "A hand-written swipe row shows its buttons under the row"). Its swipe actions are UIKit's, drawn by UIKit (rounded on iOS 26 and later) whatever the buttons paint; when every control the row names says `appearance="none"`, the paint is kept instead, in a grouped list too: the row swipes by its own scroll, as on the web, with one row open at a time (a native swipe row's opening closes it, and its drag closes a native one), a full swipe past half the row pressing the outermost action (a haptic as it arms), and each action a VoiceOver custom action of the row's content. An `image` source is the same string on every host: a path under the app's `assets/`, an `http(s)` URL, `symbol:` (the roles are [`schema.json`](../kernel/tables/schema.json)'s `symbols`; a player's are `play`, `pause`, their `-fill`s, `skip-back-15`, `skip-forward-15`, `skip-back-30`, `skip-forward-30`, `speaker`, `speaker-mute` and `moon`; an unknown role is refused with the list), `symbol:sf/` (an SF Symbol by its Apple name: drawn on Apple only, blank on the web and Linux, where `layout` reports `reason: "platform"`; a build of an app that ships either warns, its first use with the repair and each later one in a line; a tab or button that must show everywhere takes a role or an icon token), an `app:/data|cache|tmp/…` file (a picked photo, or one the data module kept with `storage.fs`; it shows after a relaunch too), or a `data:` URL of at most 1 MiB, past which every host shows nothing (the web and Apple journal `image refused`). An `iframe` of a page under `assets/` or `deck/` is given an `app:/cache` or `app:/tmp` file its `src` names in its query, encoded as any query value is: `` src=`assets/viewer/index.html?file=${encodeURIComponent(path)}` ``. The page reads `new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('file')` and gets a URL it can fetch, of any size, until the frame's `src` changes. A value naming `app:/data`, a link or a missing file is emptied (`file=`), the frame loads as usual, and the host logs why; copy the file into `app:/cache` first. An HTML, SVG or XML file is given as `application/octet-stream`, so it never runs as the app: read its bytes, into a Blob of your own for an SVG `img`, or into a `srcdoc` frame under a `sandbox` without `allow-same-origin` for HTML. The web, macOS and iOS give files; Android does not ([LLP 1020.001 D7](../llp/1020.001-a-multi-file-bundled-page-in-an-iframe.rfc.md)). Shrink a picked photo for an upload limit with `storage.fs.compressImage(path, to, {maxDimension, maxBytes})`, which writes an upright JPEG with no location metadata (`type: "image/png"` writes a PNG that keeps transparency; [reference](reference.md#shrink-a-picked-image-for-upload-storagefscompressimage)); Linux answers `unsupported`. Save an edit (a turn, a flip, a crop, a size) with `storage.fs.transformImage(path, to, {rotate, crop})`, which keeps the photo's colour, HDR and metadata where the host can and says what it wrote ([reference](reference.md#save-an-edit-of-a-photo-storagefstransformimage)); `compressImage` takes `rotate`, `flip` and `crop` too. Upload a file with `fetch(url, {method: "POST", headers: {"content-type": "image/jpeg"}, exactBodyFrom: path})`, not `readFile` then `body`: the host reads the file as it sends (under `fs.read`, at most 64 MiB), so a 2 MB photo never passes through the answer's 100 ms step; a missing or denied file rejects the fetch, naming why. To show an upload's percentage while the person goes on, make it a resource's stream with `exactUploadProgress: true`: its mapper gets `progress` (`loaded` of `total` bytes sent), then `load` with the reply's `status`, and no answer waits for it. It is asked once for its arguments while the app runs, across a reload too, though not the web JS target's development reload (a refresh or store write never sends it again, and one cut off after it began comes back failed, `interrupted`), so a retry puts an attempt number in its arguments and in its URL or a header: new arguments that make the same request keep the running upload. A launch starts afresh and sends again an upload the view still shows, so record what it answered (the server's id for the attachment) in the store and stop showing the resource once you have it ([reference](reference.md), "An upload that tells its progress"). Download a file with `fetch(url, {exactBodyTo: path})`, not `arrayBuffer()` then `writeFile`: the host writes a 2xx body into the file as it arrives (under `fs.write`, at most 1 GiB), so a large file never enters the engine's 64 MiB heap; `response.exactBodyTo.bytes` is its size, and a reply that is not 2xx leaves the file untouched and reads as usual. Keep a picked photo by copying it to `app:/data` and answering that path; never tell hosts apart in the data module (`HermesInternal`) to choose a source ([LLP 1069.002](../llp/1069.002-media-picker.rfc.md) D7, [LLP 1011](../llp/1011-image-v1.spec.md) §2). An `image` hears HTML ``'s two events, once per source, on every host: `load=` when the picture is ready (no payload), and `error=` when it does not load, with a `message` that says why (`error=failed` runs `action failed(message: string)`; `error=failed("icon")` passes `"icon"` before it). Natively the message is the reason (`HTTP 404`, `Could not connect to the server.`, `not an image format this host decodes`), and a link it quotes has no query; the browser gives none, so the web says `the image did not load`. On every native host a download that asking again may mend (the network, a lookup, TLS, a timeout, the spool, a 5xx, 408 or 429, an empty body) is asked again while the picture is on screen, after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 s and never sooner than `Retry-After`, so its `error` comes once those are spent (about a minute of waits, plus the downloads and any `Retry-After`), and one that fails off screen errs only after it has shown ([LLP 1011](../llp/1011-image-v1.spec.md) §4). A symbol fires neither. What each host's fetch of an `http(s)` source sends, follows and accepts is LLP 1011's: macOS and iOS send no cookie and no `Referer`, follow redirects to any host (within App Transport Security), take a body up to 64 MiB whatever its `Content-Type` and its status, as a browser's `` does (a 404 that is an image draws; one that is not is `HTTP 404`), and keep an HTTP cache on disk; the web is the browser's `` (its cookies and `Referer` rules, no size cap). SVG draws on the web only; on Apple it is an `error`. A tinted remote image on the web needs CORS headers, or it is an `error` too. A drive sees both after `clock + real`; `clock settle` can return just before them. ### Sound, MIDI and media

The compiler's built-in tag vocabulary is grouped here by use. It is not an
HTML parser: arbitrary HTML names outside this table are not implicitly accepted.
Several tags share a kernel node type with different fixed properties.

| Family | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Boxes / layout | `view`, `box`, `row`, `column`, `scroll`, `list` |
| Structure | `main`, `header`, `nav`, `section`, `footer`, `article`, `aside`, `dialog`, `hr` |
| Tables / description lists | `table`, `caption`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th`, `td`; `dl`, `dt`, `dd` |
| Text and controls | `text`, `h1`–`h6`, `button`, `link`, `input`, `textarea`, `select`, `option`, `progress` |
| Media / metadata | `image`, `video`, `audio`, `iframe`, `canvas`, `head` |
| SVG scene | `svg`, `g`, `path`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `rect` |
| SVG definitions | `defs`, `symbol`, `use`, `clipPath`, `marker`, `mask`, `pattern` |
| SVG color / text / embedding | `linearGradient`, `radialGradient`, `stop`, `tspan`, `foreignObject` |
| SVG filters | `filter`, `feBlend`, `feColorMatrix`, `feComponentTransfer`, `feComposite`, `feConvolveMatrix`, `feDiffuseLighting`, `feDisplacementMap`, `feDropShadow`, `feFlood`, `feFuncR`, `feFuncG`, `feFuncB`, `feFuncA`, `feGaussianBlur`, `feMerge`, `feMergeNode`, `feMorphology`, `feOffset`, `feSpecularLighting`, `feTile`, `feTurbulence`, `feDistantLight`, `fePointLight`, `feSpotLight` |

`h1` to `h6` are `text role="heading" aria-level=1` to `6` (LLP 1116.017 D1). `text` inside SVG has SVG semantics. A hyphenated tag names a native module: the
bake checks it against `app.json`'s `modules` list (`bake-unknown-module`), and
its unknown attributes, and an SVG element's own props, pass to the module as one
object. A known attribute binds to the module's box, and the box takes only layout,
box and paint rows, handlers, `testId`, `id`, `class`, `data-*`, `role`, ARIA,
`disabled` and `inert`; any other known name (`color`, `value`, `command`, `href`)
is `lower-native-attr` (LLP 1024 D1, LLP 1088 D7.2). A capitalized name is a component use, not a
built-in tag. Platform support can further restrict an admitted tag, notably
native `foreignObject`.

seekOffset: number, seekTime: number, fastSeek: bool }` to an action that takes
one: `seekOffset` is the platform's, else the element's `seekbackwardOffset` or
`seekforwardOffset` (seconds, greater than 0, default 10), 0 for the other four;
`seekTime` is `seekto`'s. An action or an offset on an element without
`metadata=` is `lower-media-session`. The platform's play and pause act on the
element, whose own `play` and `pause` events report them; the session's position
and playback state are the player's. Of several claimants, the one that most
recently started playing owns the session (else the latest mounted).
`scroll` appends left then top offsets, and to an action that takes one more
parameter a `ScrollEvent`: the scroller's own `scrollLeft`, `scrollTop`,
`scrollWidth`, `scrollHeight`, `clientWidth` and `clientHeight` as the event
fires, what a web handler reads off `event.target`. "At the end" is the web's
arithmetic, on every host and on a virtualized list too (chat F4, a
jump-to-latest pill); a native host's `scrollHeight` is its port plus the range
it clamps to:

```text
action moved(x: number, y: number, e: ScrollEvent)
  away = e.scrollHeight - e.scrollTop - e.clientHeight > 1
list appearance="none" virtualized=true scroll-start="end" scrollFollowEnd=true scroll=moved …
```

On a virtualized list, the record also carries `firstVisibleKey: option<string>`
and `firstVisibleOffset: number`: the first row intersecting the port, and the
signed distance in CSS pixels from its wrapper's start to the port's start,
on the list's axis. Keys are text (numeric and boolean keys use their text
representation). The snapshot uses the event's offset and the list's latest
measured/estimated sizes; zero-size rows are skipped. An ordinary scroller,
an empty list, or a port showing only padding reports `none` and `0`.

The app can save these two fields by document or conversation and restore
after mounting the list with `scrollIntoView("feed", key, offset=within)`.
`offset=` is a finite number and belongs only to the list form. It places the
port that many pixels into the keyed row wrapper, overriding that list's
`block`/`inline` alignment and scroll-padding, clamped to the scroll range.

48:## Paging columns
49-
50-A masonry has no collection edges: `reachstart` and `reachend` are
51-refused. Put one `intersect=` marker after the columns, inside their scroller:
52-
53-```contract
54-component Feed
55-  state cards = [0, 1, 2]
56-  action loadMore(entry: IntersectionObserverEntry)
57-    if entry.isIntersecting and cards.length < 12
58-      let next = cards.length
59-      cards = cards.concat([next, next + 1, next + 2])
60-  view
61-    scroll height="100%"
62-      row align-items="flex-start" gap=16
63-        for col in [0, 1, 2] key=col
64-          column flex=1 min-width=0 gap=8
65-            for card in cards.filter(n => n % 3 == col) key=card
66-              text `Card ${card + 1}` padding=16 testId=`card-${card}`
67-      if cards.length < 12
68-        for boundary in [cards.length] key=boundary
69-          view intersect=loadMore intersect-margin="0px 0px 800px 0px"
70-            height=1 testId="load-more"
71-```
72-
73-Ignore leave notifications; remount the keyed marker after appending to fill a
74-short page. Remove it at the end. A server feed also skips while a request is
75-pending and rekeys only after appending its answer.
76-[Delivery rules](../reference.md#intersection-visibility).
"snapshot"

bun exact.mjs ios [--run|--prebuild] [--release] [--sim <udid|name>] [--device [--phone <udid|name>]] [--url <url>]
  build for an iOS simulator and install it (--run launches it)

  --run                  also launch it (in Simulator.app, or on the phone); returns once launched
  --prebuild             start the build apart from this shell and return; its log: .exact/<ios|macos>-build.log
  --release              the build that ships, as EXACT_UPDATE_TRUST=production: it ignores EXACT_AGENT and EXACT_MODULES, so drive the development build; a first is minutes: --prebuild --release early, then --release waits for it and takes seconds; an iOS agent drive installs over it, saying how to put it back
  --sim <udid|name>      which simulator (else EXACT_SIM, a booted iPhone, or the newest Pro)
  --device               a connected iPhone, signed with a development profile on this Mac
  --phone <udid|name>    which phone, with --device
  --archive <out.ipa>    with --device: an .ipa to distribute (EXACT_IDENTITY, EXACT_PROFILE), no phone; production trust, so with an update store EXACT_UPDATE_RECEIPT or EXACT_UPDATE_GENESIS=1
  --unsigned             with --archive: ad-hoc signed, for a service that re-signs it
  --tvos                 an Apple TV simulator instead (with --device, an Apple TV)
  --url <url>            connect the client to that dev server (web's URL) for live reload
  --optimize speed|size  the Rust archive's (default speed, or app.json host.ios|macos.optimize)

The first build takes minutes, later ones a minute or two. Of several booted simulators it
takes the one the app is installed on, else refuses to guess (--sim or EXACT_SIM). test ios
and agent ios run it first themselves when the build is missing or older than its sources;
an edit to only app.contract or what app.ts imports runs its new plan on the existing build
instead, in about a second.
Ports    none. Runs to completion (--run too); --prebuild returns at once, the build going on
         apart from this shell (its pid printed; test, agent and ios without it wait for it).
Example  bun exact.mjs ios --run

# Recipe: app.json, assets and modules

`app.json` names the app and what it ships; its `$schema` gives an editor every key.

```json
{
  "$schema": "../exact2/scripts/app.schema.json",
  "app": { "id": "com.yourcompany.euxy", "name": "Euxy" },
  "name": "Euxy",
  "modules": ["waveform-view"],
  "audio_session": "playback",
  "icons": [{ "src": "assets/icon-1024.png", "sizes": "1024x1024", "type": "image/png" }],
  "protocol_handlers": [{ "protocol": "euxy", "url": "/p/%s" }]
}
```

```contract
sound "assets/tick.wav"

component App
  action tick
    playSound("assets/tick.wav")
  view
    column
      image "assets/logo.png" width=96 object-fit="contain" aria-label="Euxy"
      button press=tick testId="tick"
        text "Tick"
```

- **`assets/`** ships whole on every host. Contract names a file by its path from the app
  (no leading slash): `image "assets/logo.png"`, a `sound` and `playSound`, a `font` block's
  `400 = "assets/Inter-Regular.ttf"` (then `font-family="Inter"`).
- **`modules/apple/*.swift`** (or `*.xcframework`) is the app's native module;
  `modules/web/index.js` answers on the web ([native-module](native-module.md)). `modules`
  lists the hyphenated tags of native views ([native-views](native-views.md)): a tag the
  list lacks is `bake-unknown-module`.
- **`audio_session`**: `"playback"` where sound is the point (the silent switch leaves it
  on); the default `ambient` mixes with other audio.
- **`app.id` and `app.name`** are set before the first build (`exact new --name --bundle-id`,
  [porting-and-release](porting-and-release.md)); `app.ts` takes the id from here.
- **`host.ios.launchImage`** `{ "src": "assets/splash.png", "width": 276 }`: the launch
  screen's PNG, `width` points wide, on `background_color`.
- **`host.ios.icon`** `"art/App.icon"`: an Icon Composer `.icon`; the web keeps `icons`.
- **`protocol_handlers`**: `euxy://p/abc` is `/p/euxy%3A%2F%2Fp%2Fabc` (whole at `%s`).
  A cold launch opens it in its route's tab: declare it (`p "/p/:d"`). Running, `go`
  pushes it on the selected tab; `open` uses its route's (`vocab navigate`).
- **Other keys:** `icons`, `data` (the `data-*` words a hatch reads), `tamber` (the design's
  file), `strings` (string tables), `typescript.sources` (outside directories `app.ts`
  imports), `commands` (the app's own `exact.mjs` verbs), `env` (settings read at build and
  inlined into the module on every host, so a secret does not belong there:
  [rest-backend](rest-backend.md)).
- **`host.ios.appClip`** `{}`: the app as an App Clip too (`id` defaults to `<app id>.Clip`;
  each `applinks:` domain is its `appclips:` one).
- **Not here:** grants (in `app.ts`), fonts and sounds (Contract).
- **A change to `app.json`, `assets/`, Swift, grants, `appId`, fonts or strings rebuilds** the
  native app (`bun exact.mjs ios`). An edit to `.contract` files, to `app.ts` (short of its
  grants, `appId` and canvas surfaces) or what it imports reaches a running build in seconds;
  with a Rust data crate, a file the build reads rebuilds ([ios-driving](ios-driving.md)).

content.content:
image: tag, Image (html); positional imageSource
image: prop attribute
  prop headImage, str
  only on `head`

scroll: tag, ScrollView (html)
  A box whose content scrolls inside its bound: give it one (a `height`, or `flex=1 min-height=0` in a flex column that has one). In a route it is the navigation bar's scroller (`navigationScroll` on the route names another by its `id`). `scroll document` (or `document=(expr)`) makes it the web page's own scroll: the page scrolls, not the box, so the mobile browser's toolbar collapses and `#id` anchors, printing and scroll restoration work. A website's pages each use one; in a stack that keeps its routes mounted (`for e in stack(nav)`), each route keeps its own place in the page's scroll. Natively it scrolls as without `document`. docs/patterns/site/app.contract
scroll: handler attribute
  `scroll=act` calls `action act(scrollLeft: number, scrollTop: number)`, or `action act(scrollLeft: number, scrollTop: number, event: ScrollEvent)` for its `ScrollEvent`
  event scroll
scroll: a value of `background-attachment`, `overflow`, `overflow-x`, `overflow-y` (`contract vocab background-attachment` lists the others)

scroll (a concept): scrolling to the top, or to an item
From an action, `scrollIntoView(id)` scrolls every scroller above the element with that `id`
until it shows, as the web's `Element.scrollIntoView()` does: `block="start"` by default
(`"center"`, `"end"`, `"nearest"`), `behavior="smooth"` to animate. The top is the first
element's `id`; an item is its own.

```contract
component App
  state rows = ["Apples", "Bread", "Milk", "Tea", "Eggs"]
  action toTop
    scrollIntoView("top", behavior="smooth")
  action toItem(r: string)
    scrollIntoView(`row-${r}`, block="center")
  view
    column height="100%" display="flex" flex-direction="column"
      row gap=8 padding=8
        button press=toTop testId="to-top"
          text "Top"
        button press=toItem("Tea") testId="to-tea"
          text "Tea"
      scroll flex=1 min-height=0
        text "Groceries" id="top" role="heading" aria-level=2 padding=16
        for r in rows key=r
          text r id=`row-${r}` padding=16
```

- Every scroller above the element moves, so a horizontal strip inside a sheet or a form
  scrolls the form too. `block="nearest"` leaves a scroller that already shows the element
  where it is, and `inline` (`"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, default `"nearest"`) places it
  across a horizontal strip: ``scrollIntoView(`icon-${i}`, block="nearest", inline="start")``.
- A virtualized `list` (rows not built yet) scrolls to a row by its key:
  `scrollIntoView("list-id", key, block="center")`. A chat opens at its newest row with
  `scroll-start="end"` on a `list virtualized=true`, and `scrollFollowEnd=true` keeps it
  there as messages arrive, while the reader is at the end (`chat-thread`; a grouped list
  is never virtualized).
  To restore after remount, save `ScrollEvent.firstVisibleKey` and
  `firstVisibleOffset` in the app, then call `scrollIntoView("list-id", key, offset=within)`.
  The optional key is text; the offset is signed CSS pixels into the row on the list's axis.
- `scrollTop=y` on a scroller moves it only when `y` changes, so a second "top" does
  nothing; `scroll=moved` reports the offset (`action moved(x: number, y: number)`).

More: docs/contract-grammar.md#host-commands (`scrollIntoView`)

list: tag, List (html); sets accessibilityRole=list

```contract
  state rows = ["Apples", "Bread", "Milk", "Tea", "Eggs"]
  action toTop
    scrollIntoView("top", behavior="smooth")
  action toItem(r: string)
    scrollIntoView(`row-${r}`, block="center")
  view
    column height="100%" display="flex" flex-direction="column"
      row gap=8 padding=8
        button press=toTop testId="to-top"
          text "Top"
        button press=toItem("Tea") testId="to-tea"
          text "Tea"
      scroll flex=1 min-height=0
        text "Groceries" id="top" role="heading" aria-level=2 padding=16
        for r in rows key=r
          text r id=`row-${r}` padding=16
```

- Every scroller above the element moves, so a horizontal strip inside a sheet or a form
  scrolls the form too. `block="nearest"` leaves a scroller that already shows the element
  where it is, and `inline` (`"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, default `"nearest"`) places it
  across a horizontal strip: ``scrollIntoView(`icon-${i}`, block="nearest", inline="start")``.
- A virtualized `list` (rows not built yet) scrolls to a row by its key:
  `scrollIntoView("list-id", key, block="center")`. A chat opens at its newest row with
  `scroll-start="end"` on a `list virtualized=true`, and `scrollFollowEnd=true` keeps it
  there as messages arrive, while the reader is at the end (`chat-thread`; a grouped list
  is never virtualized).
  To restore after remount, save `ScrollEvent.firstVisibleKey` and
  `firstVisibleOffset` in the app, then call `scrollIntoView("list-id", key, offset=within)`.
  The optional key is text; the offset is signed CSS pixels into the row on the list's axis.
- `scrollTop=y` on a scroller moves it only when `y` changes, so a second "top" does
  nothing; `scroll=moved` reports the offset (`action moved(x: number, y: number)`).

content.content:
scroll-snap-align: style attribute
  rows scroll_snap_align
  enum none|start|end, default none

task (a concept): a timer, once or repeating (every, after)
A root `task` has one schedule: `every(ms, action)` repeats, `after(ms, action)` fires once,
`every(frame, action)` ticks once a display frame. `task t mount` runs from launch; `task t
when cond` only while `cond` holds, and `key=x` restarts it when `x` changes. The interval is
a literal number of milliseconds, and the action takes no parameters.

```contract
component App
  state seconds = 0
  task t mount
    every(1000, tick)
  action tick
    seconds = floor(performanceNow() / 1000)
  view
    text `${seconds}s` testId="n"
```

- A `derive` that reads `performanceNow()` is not read again as time passes: the tick's action
  writes it to state. In a test `clock +N` fires the timers; never wait in real time.
- Measure time, never count ticks: on a device, ticks missed while the app was suspended fire
  once, not once each.

More: docs/recipes/timers.md

safe-area (a concept): the notch, the status bar and the home indicator
Inside a route, leave it unsaid: the host keeps the route's content clear of the status bar
and its bars (UIKit's inset on the route's scroller, else the route's padding), and a
scroller's end clear of the home indicator, as a hand-built screen is. `env()` is CSS's, in
any length (`padding-bottom="calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 16px)"`). On a native host
under the default `viewport-fit="auto"` it is 0, so `env()` padding inside a route adds
nothing; under the root's `viewport-fit="cover"` it is the device's insets, and a route's
content goes under the bar unless its column pads `env(safe-area-inset-top)`. On the web it is
the browser's. `env(-exact-layout-margins-inset-left)` is UIKit's layout margin.

- A scroller's last row sits its `padding-bottom` above UIKit's inset: subtract the inset
  from the original's gap rather than adding `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.

More: docs/agent-pitfalls.md ("Native presentation and navigation (iOS)"), docs/contract-grammar.md (length strings)

A title button keeps its contents; an authored Back replaces UIKit Back. Search or a header tablist can opt out on that element; a tab button alone keeps its parent segmented. // Everbloom: the view. app.ts answers what it asks for (the Storefront API).
use openBrowser, BrowserResult from "@exact/in-app-browser"
use Icon, BackIcon, ProductCard, MiniCard, Skeleton, ErrorState, Spinner from "./parts.contract"
use Card, CardRow, ResultRow, ProductDetail, Variant from "./shapes.contract"
use ProductScreen from "./product.contract"

routes nav
  tab home "/"
    collection "/collection/:handle"
    product "/product/:handle"
  tab search "/search"
  tab cart "/cart"

shape Collection
  id: string
  handle: string
  title: string
  banner: string
  image: string

shape Home
  loaded: bool
  collections: Collection[]
  best: Card[]

shape CollectionPage
  key: string
  loaded: bool
  title: string
  description: string
  hasNext: bool
  rows: CardRow[]

shape SearchPage
  query: string
  loaded: bool
  total: number
  hasNext: bool
  results: ResultRow[]

shape Products
  items: ProductDetail[]

shape Line
  id: string
  index: number
  title: string
  variant: string
  image: string
  quantity: number
  total: string

shape Cart
  id: string
  checkoutUrl: string
  totalQuantity: number
  subtotal: string
  lines: Line[]

shape CartReply
  seq: number
  ok: bool
  error: string
  cart: Cart

shape Ack
  ok: bool

shape SortChip
  id: string
  label: string

fn sortChips(): SortChip[] = [SortChip(id="featured", label="Featured"), SortChip(id="best-selling", label="Best selling"), SortChip(id="price-asc", label="Price: low to high"), SortChip(id="price-desc", label="Price: high to low")]
fn collectionTitle(cs: Collection[], handle: string): string = match first(cs.filter(c => c.handle == handle)) { case some(c) => c.title, case none => "" }
fn emptyCart(): Cart = Cart(id="", checkoutUrl="", totalQuantity=0, subtotal="$0.00", lines=[])

component App
  state sort = "featured"
  state pages = 1
  state query = ""
  state submitted = ""
  state searchPages = 1
  state goCartAfter = false
  state readyLogged = false
  state alertText = ""
  derive collectionHandle = match first(first(nav.tabs.filter(t => t.name == "home")).map(t => t.stack).flat().filter(e => e.name == "collection")) { case some(e) => e.params.handle, case none => "" }
  derive productHandles = nav.tabs.map(t => t.stack.filter(e => e.name == "product").map(e => e.params.handle)).flat()
  resource home = loadHome() as shape Home else empty(loaded=false)
  resource coll = loadCollection(collectionHandle, sort, pages) as shape CollectionPage else empty(loaded=false)
  resource found = searchProducts(submitted, searchPages) as shape SearchPage else empty(loaded=false)
  resource products = loadProducts(productHandles) as shape Products else empty()
  mutation cartOp as shape CartReply queue then afterCart
  mutation logged as shape Ack
  mutation browsed as shape BrowserResult
  derive cart = match cartOp { case some(r) => r.cart, case none => emptyCart() }
  derive collKey = `${collectionHandle}|${sort}`
  derive collReady = coll.loaded and coll.key == collKey
  derive searchReady = found.loaded and found.query == submitted.trim()
  derive hideTabs = top(nav).name == "product"

  task ready when home.loaded and not readyLogged
    after(1, markReady)
  task debounce when query != submitted key=query
    after(300, commitQuery)

  action markReady
    readyLogged = true
    send logged = homeReady()
  action pick(name: string)
    nav = select(nav, name)
  action follow(url: string)
    nav = go(nav, url)
  action goBack
    nav = back(nav)
  action openCollection(handle: string)
    sort = "featured"
    pages = 1
    nav = push(nav, path("collection", handle))
  action openProduct(handle: string)
    nav = push(nav, path("product", handle))
  action retryHome
    refresh home
  action pickSort(id: string)
    sort = id
    pages = 1
  action moreCollection
    if collReady and coll.hasNext and not pending(coll) and not failed(coll)
      pages = pages + 1
  action retryCollection
    refresh coll
  action typed(v: string)
    query = v
  action commitQuery
    submitted = query
    searchPages = 1
  action moreSearch
    if searchReady and found.hasNext and not pending(found) and not failed(found)
      searchPages = searchPages + 1
  action retrySearch
    refresh found
  action retryProducts
    refresh products
  action add(variantId: string)
    goCartAfter = true
    send cartOp = addToCart(variantId)
  action setQuantity(lineId: string, quantity: number)
    send cartOp = updateLine(lineId, quantity)
  action afterCart
    match cartOp
      case some(r)
        if r.error != ""
          alertText = r.error
          goCartAfter = false
          showModal("cart-alert")
        else if goCartAfter
          goCartAfter = false
          nav = select(nav, "cart")
      case none
        goCartAfter = false

    if cart.checkoutUrl != ""
      send browsed = openBrowser(url=cart.checkoutUrl)

// Everbloom: the view. app.ts answers what it asks for (the Storefront API).
use openBrowser, BrowserResult from "@exact/in-app-browser"
use Icon, BackIcon, ProductCard, MiniCard, Skeleton, ErrorState, Spinner from "./parts.contract"
use Card, CardRow, ResultRow, ProductDetail, Variant from "./shapes.contract"
use ProductScreen from "./product.contract"

routes nav
  tab home "/"
    collection "/collection/:handle"
    product "/product/:handle"
  tab search "/search"
  tab cart "/cart"

shape Collection
  id: string
  handle: string
  title: string
  banner: string
  image: string

shape Home
  loaded: bool
  collections: Collection[]
  best: Card[]

shape CollectionPage
  key: string
  loaded: bool
  title: string
  description: string
  hasNext: bool
  rows: CardRow[]

shape SearchPage
  query: string
  loaded: bool
  total: number
  hasNext: bool
  results: ResultRow[]

shape Products
  items: ProductDetail[]

shape Line
  id: string
  index: number
  title: string
  variant: string
  image: string
  quantity: number
  total: string

shape Cart
  id: string
  checkoutUrl: string
  totalQuantity: number
  subtotal: string
  lines: Line[]

shape CartReply
  seq: number
  ok: bool
  error: string
  cart: Cart

shape Ack
  ok: bool

shape SortChip
  id: string
  label: string

fn sortChips(): SortChip[] = [SortChip(id="featured", label="Featured"), SortChip(id="best-selling", label="Best selling"), SortChip(id="price-asc", label="Price: low to high"), SortChip(id="price-desc", label="Price: high to low")]
fn collectionTitle(cs: Collection[], handle: string): string = match first(cs.filter(c => c.handle == handle)) { case some(c) => c.title, case none => "" }
fn emptyCart(): Cart = Cart(id="", checkoutUrl="", totalQuantity=0, subtotal="$0.00", lines=[])

component App
  state sort = "featured"
  state pages = 1
  state query = ""
  state submitted = ""
  state searchPages = 1
  state goCartAfter = false
  state readyLogged = false
  state alertText = ""
  derive collectionHandle = match first(first(nav.tabs.filter(t => t.name == "home")).map(t => t.stack).flat().filter(e => e.name == "collection")) { case some(e) => e.params.handle, case none => "" }
  derive productHandles = nav.tabs.map(t => t.stack.filter(e => e.name == "product").map(e => e.params.handle)).flat()
  resource home = loadHome() as shape Home else empty(loaded=false)
  resource coll = loadCollection(collectionHandle, sort, pages) as shape CollectionPage else empty(loaded=false)
  resource found = searchProducts(submitted, searchPages) as shape SearchPage else empty(loaded=false)
  resource products = loadProducts(productHandles) as shape Products else empty()
  mutation cartOp as shape CartReply queue then afterCart
  mutation logged as shape Ack
  mutation browsed as shape BrowserResult
  derive cart = match cartOp { case some(r) => r.cart, case none => emptyCart() }
  derive collKey = `${collectionHandle}|${sort}`
  derive collReady = coll.loaded and coll.key == collKey
  derive searchReady = found.loaded and found.query == submitted.trim()
  derive hideTabs = top(nav).name == "product"

  task ready when home.loaded and not readyLogged
    after(1, markReady)
  task debounce when query != submitted key=query
    after(300, commitQuery)

  action markReady
    readyLogged = true
    send logged = homeReady()
  action pick(name: string)
    nav = select(nav, name)
  action follow(url: string)
    nav = go(nav, url)
  action goBack
    nav = back(nav)
  action openCollection(handle: string)
    sort = "featured"
    pages = 1
    nav = push(nav, path("collection", handle))
  action openProduct(handle: string)
    nav = push(nav, path("product", handle))
  action retryHome
    refresh home
  action pickSort(id: string)
    sort = id
    pages = 1
  action moreCollection
    if collReady and coll.hasNext and not pending(coll) and not failed(coll)
      pages = pages + 1
  action retryCollection
    refresh coll
  action typed(v: string)
    query = v
  action commitQuery
    submitted = query
    searchPages = 1
  action moreSearch
    if searchReady and found.hasNext and not pending(found) and not failed(found)
      searchPages = searchPages + 1
  action retrySearch
    refresh found
  action retryProducts
    refresh products
  action add(variantId: string)
    goCartAfter = true
    send cartOp = addToCart(variantId)
  action setQuantity(lineId: string, quantity: number)
    send cartOp = updateLine(lineId, quantity)
  action afterCart
    match cartOp
      case some(r)
        if r.error != ""
          alertText = r.error
          goCartAfter = false
          showModal("cart-alert")
        else if goCartAfter
          goCartAfter = false
          nav = select(nav, "cart")
      case none
        goCartAfter = false
  action checkout
    if cart.checkoutUrl != ""
      send browsed = openBrowser(url=cart.checkoutUrl)
  action shop
    nav = select(nav, "home")

  view
    main viewport-fit="cover" navigationKey=`${top(nav).id}` navigationBack="back" navigate=follow testId="app"
      width="100%" height="100%" display="flex" flex-direction="column" background-color="#FFFFFF" color="#1C1B19"
      column flex=1 min-height=0 position="relative"

                          row gap=8 padding-top=8 padding-bottom=12 padding-left=16 padding-right=16
                            for c, i in home.collections key=c.id
                              button press=openCollection(c.handle) testId=`collection-chip-${i}` aria-label=c.title appearance="none"
                                flex-shrink=0 height=36 padding-left=14 padding-right=14 border-radius=999 background-color="#F4F1EC"
                                display="flex" align-items="center"
                                text c.title font-size=14 font-weight=500 white-space="nowrap" color="#1C1B19"
                        for c in home.collections.slice(0, 1) key=c.id
                          button press=openCollection(c.handle) testId="featured-collection" aria-label=c.title appearance="none"
                            margin-top=4 margin-left=16 margin-right=16 height=240 border-radius=12 overflow="hidden"
                            position="relative" background-color="#F4F1EC" display="block" text-align="start"
                            image c.banner width="100%" height="100%" object-fit="cover" object-position="center 30%" alt=""
                            column position="absolute" left=0 right=0 bottom=0 padding=16 gap=2 background-color="rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.72)"
                              text "FEATURED COLLECTION" font-size=12 font-weight=600 letter-spacing=0.6 color="#FFFFFF"
                              text c.title font-size=20 font-weight=700 color="#FFFFFF"
                              text "Shop now" font-size=14 color="#FFFFFF"
                        row padding-top=28 padding-bottom=12 padding-left=16 padding-right=16
                          text "Collections" role="heading" aria-level=2 font-size=17 font-weight=700

                                flex-shrink=0 width=140 display="flex" flex-direction="column" gap=8 text-align="start"
                                image c.image width=140 height=175 object-fit="cover" border-radius=8 background-color="#F4F1EC" alt=""
                                text c.title font-size=14 font-weight=600 line-height=18 color="#1C1B19"
                        row padding-top=28 padding-bottom=12 padding-left=16 padding-right=16
                          text "Best sellers" role="heading" aria-level=2 font-size=17 font-weight=700
                        view display="grid" grid-template-columns="minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr)" column-gap=12 row-gap=20
                          padding-left=16 padding-right=16
                          for p in home.best key=p.id
                            ProductCard(card=p, testId=`best-seller-${p.index}`, open=openProduct)
                  else if failed(home) and not pending(home)

// Everbloom: the view. app.ts answers what it asks for (the Storefront API).
use openBrowser, BrowserResult from "@exact/in-app-browser"
use Icon, BackIcon, ProductCard, MiniCard, Skeleton, ErrorState, Spinner from "./parts.contract"
use Card, CardRow, ResultRow, ProductDetail, Variant from "./shapes.contract"
use ProductScreen from "./product.contract"

routes nav
  tab home "/"
    collection "/collection/:handle"
    product "/product/:handle"
  tab search "/search"
  tab cart "/cart"

shape Collection
  id: string
  handle: string
  title: string
  banner: string
  image: string

shape Home
  loaded: bool
  collections: Collection[]
  best: Card[]

shape CollectionPage
  key: string
  loaded: bool
  title: string
  description: string
  hasNext: bool
  rows: CardRow[]

shape SearchPage
  query: string
  loaded: bool
  total: number
  hasNext: bool
  results: ResultRow[]

shape Products
  items: ProductDetail[]

shape Line
  id: string
  index: number
  title: string
  variant: string
  image: string
  quantity: number
  total: string

shape Cart
  id: string
  checkoutUrl: string
  totalQuantity: number
  subtotal: string
  lines: Line[]

shape CartReply
  seq: number
  ok: bool
  error: string
  cart: Cart

shape Ack
  ok: bool

shape SortChip
  id: string
  label: string

fn sortChips(): SortChip[] = [SortChip(id="featured", label="Featured"), SortChip(id="best-selling", label="Best selling"), SortChip(id="price-asc", label="Price: low to high"), SortChip(id="price-desc", label="Price: high to low")]
fn collectionTitle(cs: Collection[], handle: string): string = match first(cs.filter(c => c.handle == handle)) { case some(c) => c.title, case none => "" }
fn emptyCart(): Cart = Cart(id="", checkoutUrl="", totalQuantity=0, subtotal="$0.00", lines=[])

component App
  state sort = "featured"
  state pages = 1
  state query = ""
  state submitted = ""
  state searchPages = 1
  state goCartAfter = false
  state readyLogged = false
  state alertText = ""
  derive collectionHandle = match first(first(nav.tabs.filter(t => t.name == "home")).map(t => t.stack).flat().filter(e => e.name == "collection")) { case some(e) => e.params.handle, case none => "" }
  derive productHandles = nav.tabs.map(t => t.stack.filter(e => e.name == "product").map(e => e.params.handle)).flat()
  resource home = loadHome() as shape Home else empty(loaded=false)
  resource coll = loadCollection(collectionHandle, sort, pages) as shape CollectionPage else empty(loaded=false)
  resource found = searchProducts(submitted, searchPages) as shape SearchPage else empty(loaded=false)
  resource products = loadProducts(productHandles) as shape Products else empty()
  mutation cartOp as shape CartReply queue then afterCart
  mutation logged as shape Ack
  mutation browsed as shape BrowserResult
  derive cart = match cartOp { case some(r) => r.cart, case none => emptyCart() }
  derive collKey = `${collectionHandle}|${sort}`
  derive collReady = coll.loaded and coll.key == collKey
  derive searchReady = found.loaded and found.query == submitted.trim()
  derive hideTabs = top(nav).name == "product"

  task ready when home.loaded and not readyLogged
    after(1, markReady)
  task debounce when query != submitted key=query
    after(300, commitQuery)

  action markReady
    readyLogged = true
    send logged = homeReady()
  action pick(name: string)
    nav = select(nav, name)
  action follow(url: string)
    nav = go(nav, url)
  action goBack
    nav = back(nav)
  action openCollection(handle: string)
    sort = "featured"
    pages = 1
    nav = push(nav, path("collection", handle))
  action openProduct(handle: string)
    nav = push(nav, path("product", handle))
  action retryHome
    refresh home
  action pickSort(id: string)
    sort = id
    pages = 1
  action moreCollection
    if collReady and coll.hasNext and not pending(coll) and not failed(coll)
      pages = pages + 1
  action retryCollection
    refresh coll
  action typed(v: string)
    query = v
  action commitQuery
    submitted = query
    searchPages = 1
  action moreSearch
    if searchReady and found.hasNext and not pending(found) and not failed(found)
      searchPages = searchPages + 1
  action retrySearch
    refresh found
  action retryProducts
    refresh products
  action add(variantId: string)
    goCartAfter = true
    send cartOp = addToCart(variantId)
  action setQuantity(lineId: string, quantity: number)
    send cartOp = updateLine(lineId, quantity)
  action afterCart
    match cartOp
      case some(r)
        if r.error != ""
          alertText = r.error
          goCartAfter = false
          showModal("cart-alert")
        else if goCartAfter
          goCartAfter = false
          nav = select(nav, "cart")
      case none
        goCartAfter = false
  action checkout
    if cart.checkoutUrl != ""
      send browsed = openBrowser(url=cart.checkoutUrl)
  action shop
    nav = select(nav, "home")

// Everbloom: the view. app.ts answers what it asks for. Colours, fonts,
// sizes and the safe area are left unsaid, so each platform supplies its own:
// the header is the navigation bar, its heading the title, its button a bar item.
shape Greeting
  text: string

routes nav
  home "/"

component Everbloom
  resource greeting = greeting("Everbloom") as shape Greeting
  state liked = false
  action like
    liked = not liked
  view
    main testId="root" navigationKey=`${top(nav).id}` navigationBack="back" width="100%" height="100%"
      for e in stack(nav) key=e.id
        column navigationKey=`${e.id}` navigationScroll="content" position="absolute" inset=0 display="flex" flex-direction="column"
          header display="flex" align-items="center"
            text "Everbloom" role="heading" aria-level=1 flex=1
            button press=like aria-label=(liked ? "Unlike" : "Like") testId="like"
              image (liked ? "symbol:heart-fill" : "symbol:heart")
          scroll id="content" flex=1 min-height=0 padding=16
            text greeting.text testId="greeting"

component Icon
  props
    name: string
    size: number
    stroke: number
  view
    svg width=size height=size viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width=stroke stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" flex-shrink=0
      if name == "home"
        path d="M3 10.5 12 3l9 7.5V20a1 1 0 0 1-1 1h-5v-6H9v6H4a1 1 0 0 1-1-1z"
      else if name == "search"
        circle cx=11 cy=11 r=7
        path d="m20 20-3.5-3.5"
      else if name == "cart"
        path d="M6 7h12l-1 13H7z"
        path d="M9 7a3 3 0 0 1 6 0"
      else if name == "minus"
        path d="M5 12h14"
      else if name == "plus"
        path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"
      else if name == "alert"
        circle cx=12 cy=12 r=9
        path d="M12 7.5v5.5"
        path d="M12 16.5h.01"

component BackIcon
  props
    size: number
  view
    svg width=size height=size viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width=1.75 stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" flex-shrink=0
      path d="m15 5-7 7 7 7"

component Skeleton
  props
    width: number
    height: number
    radius: number

    view width=width height=height border-radius=radius background-color="#EDE9E3" flex-shrink=0

component Spinner
  view
    progress aria-label="Loading" testId="loading"

component Price
  props
    price: string
    compare: string
    size: number
  view
    row gap=6 align-items="baseline"
      text price font-size=size font-weight=700 color=(compare != "" ? "#B4361E" : "#1C1B19")
      if compare != ""
        text compare font-size=13 color="#6E6A63" text-decoration-line="line-through"

// A grid card: Home's best sellers and a collection's products.
component ProductCard
  props
    card: Card

    button press=open(card.handle) testId=testId aria-label=card.title appearance="none"

fn noVariant(): Variant = Variant(id="", title="", available=false, options=[], price="", compare="")

component ProductScreen
  props
    detail: ProductDetail
    scrollId: string
    busy: bool
    add: action
    open: action
    back: action
  state variantId = detail.initialVariant

  derive selected = match first(detail.variants.filter(v => v.id == variantId)) { case some(v) => v, case none => noVariant() }

  action choose(name: string, value: string)
    let exact = detail.variants.filter(v => v.options.filter(o => o.name == name ? o.value == value : o.value == valueOf(selected, o.name)).length == v.options.length)
    let loose = detail.variants.filter(v => valueOf(v, name) == value)
    variantId = match first(exact) { case some(v) => v.id, case none => match first(loose) { case some(v) => v.id, case none => variantId } }
  action paged(x: number, y: number, e: ScrollEvent)
    page = e.clientWidth > 0 ? round(x / e.clientWidth) : 0

                for img, i in detail.images key=i
                  view width=24 height=24 display="flex" align-items="center" justify-content="center"
                    view width=8 height=8 border-radius=999 background-color=(i == page ? "#1C1B19" : "rgba(28, 27, 25, 0.25)")

            text detail.title role="heading" aria-level=1 font-size=22 line-height=28 font-weight=700 testId="product-title"

              text selected.price font-size=20 font-weight=700 color=(selected.compare != "" ? "#B4361E" : "#1C1B19") testId="product-price"
              if selected.compare != ""
                text selected.compare font-size=15 color="#6E6A63" text-decoration-line="line-through" testId="product-compare"

            column padding-top=24 padding-left=16 padding-right=16
              row padding-bottom=12
                text `${o.name}: ` font-size=15 font-weight=600
                text valueOf(selected, o.name) font-size=15 color="#6E6A63" testId=`option-label-${o.name}`
              row gap=8 flex-wrap="wrap"
                for v in o.values key=v
                  button press=choose(o.name, v) testId=`option-${o.name}-${v}` aria-label=`${o.name} ${v}` aria-pressed=(valueOf(selected, o.name) == v) appearance="none"
                    min-width=56 height=44 padding-left=16 padding-right=16 box-sizing="border-box" border-radius=12 border-style="solid"
                    border-width=(valueOf(selected, o.name) == v ? 2 : 1) border-color=(valueOf(selected, o.name) == v ? "#1C1B19" : "#E6E1D9")
                    background-color="#FFFFFF" display="flex" align-items="center" justify-content="center"
                    text v font-size=15 font-weight=(valueOf(selected, o.name) == v ? 600 : 500) color="#1C1B19" white-space="nowrap"
          column padding-top=24 padding-left=16 padding-right=16 gap=8
            text "Description" role="heading" aria-level=2 font-size=15 font-weight=600
            text detail.description font-size=15 line-height=22 color="#3D3A35"
          if detail.recs.length > 0
            column padding-top=32
              text "You may also like" role="heading" aria-level=2 font-size=17 font-weight=700 padding-left=16 padding-right=16 padding-bottom=12
              scroll overflow-x="auto" overflow-y="hidden"
                row gap=12 padding-left=16 padding-right=16 align-items="flex-start"
                  for r in detail.recs key=r.id
                    MiniCard(card=r, testId=`recommendation-${r.index}`, open=open)
      button id="back" press=back testId="back" aria-label="Back" appearance="none"
        position="absolute" top="env(safe-area-inset-top)" left=12 width=40 height=40 border-radius=999
        background-color="#FFFFFF" display="flex" align-items="center" justify-content="center" color="#1C1B19"
        BackIcon(size=22)
      view padding-top=12 padding-left=16 padding-right=16 padding-bottom="calc(12px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))"
        background-color="#FFFFFF" border-top-width=1 border-top-style="solid" border-top-color="#E6E1D9"
        button press=addSelected disabled=(busy or selected.id == "") testId="add-to-cart" appearance="none"
          height=52 border-radius=12 background-color="#1C1B19" opacity=(busy ? 0.6 : 1)
          display="flex" align-items="center" justify-content="center"
          text `Add to cart · ${selected.price}` font-size=16 font-weight=600 color="#FFFFFF"

content.text: Store "0" means no over-the-air update checks — good for the benchmark. Writing the device build script now.

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
# The benchmarked build: Everbloom for arm64 iOS devices, release (production) mode.
#
#   DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 scripts/build-ios-device.sh   signed for that team (automatic signing)
#   scripts/build-ios-device.sh                               no team: code signing disabled (ad-hoc, for re-signing)
#
# Result: build/ios-device/Everbloom.app (and build/ios-device/Everbloom.ipa).
#
# Exact assembles and signs its .app itself (no Xcode project). For automatic
# signing, Xcode first builds a stub app with the same bundle id under
# DEVELOPMENT_TEAM with -allowProvisioningUpdates, which makes Xcode create (or
# refresh) the team's development profile for the id and every registered
# device; Exact's build then signs with that profile and the team's Apple
# Development identity.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$ROOT/everbloom"
OUT="$ROOT/build/ios-device"
BUNDLE_ID="dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact"
BUN="${BUN:-$HOME/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun}"
export PATH="$(dirname "$BUN"):$PATH"

mkdir -p "$OUT"
rm -rf "$OUT/Everbloom.app" "$OUT/Everbloom.ipa" "$OUT/Payload"

if [[ -n "${DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ]]; then
  STUB_DD="$OUT/stub-derived"
  xcodebuild -project "$ROOT/scripts/signing-stub/Stub.xcodeproj" -scheme Stub -configuration Release \
    -destination generic/platform=iOS -derivedDataPath "$STUB_DD" -allowProvisioningUpdates \
    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" STUB_BUNDLE_ID="$BUNDLE_ID" build >"$OUT/stub-build.log" 2>&1 \
    || { echo "Xcode could not sign the stub for team $DEVELOPMENT_TEAM; see $OUT/stub-build.log" >&2; exit 1; }
  PROFILE="$STUB_DD/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Stub.app/embedded.mobileprovision"
  [[ -f "$PROFILE" ]] || { echo "no provisioning profile in the stub build ($PROFILE)" >&2; exit 1; }
  cp "$PROFILE" "$OUT/team.mobileprovision"
  # The identity Xcode signed the stub with: its SHA-1, as Exact's EXACT_IDENTITY takes it.
  IDENTITY="$(codesign -dvvv "$STUB_DD/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Stub.app" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=\(Apple Development: .*\)$/\1/p' | head -1)"

bun exact.mjs android [--run] [--headless]
  build the APK and install it (test, agent and verify android drive it)

  --run       launch it once installed
  --headless  build the Linux host for Android instead (agent android --headless runs it under adb shell)

Builds android/ for aarch64-linux-android, packages it with exact2's Canvas reader
(host/android) into an APK under target/android/, prints its path and installs it on the
device: ANDROID_SERIAL, else the one adb lists (with several and none named, it refuses).
With no device it builds and says so. test android and agent android drive the installed
APK and refuse one older than its sources, naming this command.
Needs    the SDK (ANDROID_HOME) with platform 37.2 and an NDK, a JDK 17+ (JAVA_HOME), once in
         this directory rustup target add aarch64-linux-android, and the Android Hermes
         bundle (~/.cache/exact/hermes-android; bun <exact2>/scripts/hermes-android.mjs).
Device   an emulator elsewhere: adb connect 127.0.0.1:<port> through an ssh tunnel to its
         adb port, then ANDROID_SERIAL=127.0.0.1:<port>.
Ports    none. Runs to completion.
Example  ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554 bun exact.mjs android && bun exact.mjs test android

# Recipe: driving iOS

**Check a screen against a reference** (the original's screenshot) with compare, not by
eye: `bun exact.mjs agent ios --touch platform … "clock settle" "screenshot
.exact/x.png compare ref/x.png"` captures as a device does, the keyboard too on a simulator it
booted (status bar: `xcrun simctl status_bar <udid> override --time 9:41`), and says where they
differ: each region by node, where its content moved, a box measured in both (`x.side.png`:
both at half size; `x.diff.png`: reference, screen, differences). Each tap is a real touch,
reaching a pull-down menu's rows, tabs and a native module's controls. A context menu, a row
scrolled out of its menu and an alert's buttons take a drive without the flag.

Edit and check on the web (`verify`); run `verify ios` once, at the end: the tests with UIKit's
bars, light and dark, and a relaunch ([tests](tests.md#before-you-call-it-done)). Drives build
first when stale; `--prebuild` starts the first early. With an `app.ts` data module, an edit to
`.contract` files, `app.ts` or what it imports reaches iOS in seconds as a baked plan (log
`.exact/ios-plan.log`); `app.json`, assets, fonts, grants, `appId`, canvas surfaces and, with a
Rust data crate, any file the build reads rebuild.

**One drive checks many screens**: `back` closes an alert or sheet or pops a screen,
`type <root> <path>` opens a route (`<root>`: the `navigate=` node's testId). A drive that
compares starts its store empty.

```sh
bun exact.mjs agent ios "clock data" "screenshot .exact/a.png compare ref/a.png" "tap add-item" \
  "clock settle" "screenshot .exact/b.png compare ref/b.png" back "type app /item/1" \
  "clock data" "clock settle" "screenshot .exact/c.png compare ref/c.png"
```

| Flag or op | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `check`, `check dark`, `check both` | What is wrong: clipped text, a covered control, a small target, low contrast. |
| `--scale 3` | Screenshots at 3 px a point, not 1. |
| `screenshot <file> window` | The whole screen, bars included; a plain one is the window's too while an alert, sheet or menu is up. `screenshot <f> over 600 every 50 window` films it. |
| `tap <id> down` `screenshot <png>` `tap up` | `<id>` shown pressed, then pressed once; `tap hold <ms>` moves the clock. |
| `clock settle` | Ends a transition, runs an `after(1, …)`; waits up to 1.5 s for UIKit's animations (4 s: a list gliding). |
| `--timing platform`, `--touch platform` | UIKit's own transition timing (default: frozen); every tap and drag a real touch. |
| `--sim <udid\|name>` (`EXACT_SIM`) | Which simulator (default: the app's). |

- Drive by `testId` (a bar button's, field's, tab's `accessibilityIdentifier`), never by
  coordinates; `tap` and `type` scroll their target into view.
- A wheel or `tap <scroller> drag 0 -300` moves content (and bars) that far; a real
  drag glides unless held 100 ms ([more](../contract-for-agents.md#drags-on-ios)).
- A tap on an alert's or action sheet's button returns once UIKit has dismissed it and the press
  lands, so a `clock data` next sees it.

# Everbloom (Exact): notes

## Layout of this repository

- `everbloom/` is the Exact app (`app.contract`, `product.contract`, `parts.contract`,
  `shapes.contract`: the view; `app.ts` + `graphql.ts`: the data module; `modules/apple/Shop.swift`:
  the iOS native module; `app.json`: the manifest).
  Exact names an app's crates after its directory, and the project root's name, `exact`,
  collides with Exact's own crates (`exact new` refuses it), so the app is one directory down.
- `vendor/exact2/` is the Exact checkout the app builds against (Exact has no releases or
  packages; an app uses a checkout by path). It is pinned to commit
  `fc14919528fb76ca8de3e8c8d9ef91853f923a17` and cloned by the install step in `BUILD.md`.
  It is not modified.
- `vendor/ibex/` is Expo's Ibex checkout (commit `a0183568e8229b8243629cdb26cd4a88ac4e2abd`),
  used only to build the Android Hermes bundle, which no Ibex release ships yet.
- `scripts/build-ios-device.sh` builds the iOS device release; `scripts/signing-stub/` is a
  never-shipped stub Xcode project used only to obtain Xcode's automatically managed
  provisioning profile for `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` (Exact assembles and signs the `.app` itself,
  without an Xcode project).

## Dependencies added

- `@exact/in-app-browser` (part of the Exact checkout, `vendor/exact2/packages/in-app-browser`):
  opens `checkoutUrl` in the platform's in-app browser (SFSafariViewController on iOS, a Custom
  Tab on Android). Contract has no built-in browser view.

No third-party packages. GraphQL is sent with plain `fetch`.

## Decisions where the spec is silent

- **Architecture.** All requests go through `app.ts`. The view declares one resource per data
  set: `loadHome`, `loadCollection(handle, sort, pages)`, `searchProducts(query, pages)` and
  `loadProducts(handles)` (every product screen on either tab's stack, so stacked product screens
  each keep their data). Infinite scroll raises `pages`; `app.ts` keeps the pages it already
  fetched in memory and fetches only the next one with `after: endCursor`. Product details are
  memoized per handle for the session (successes only, so Retry refetches a failure).
- **First page variables.** `after` is omitted from `variables` on the first page (not sent as
  `null`).
- **Stale responses.** Exact drops a resource answer whose request is no longer current, so a
  search answer for an old query never replaces the current one; the view also compares the
  answer's query with the current query.
- **Cart.** The cart id is kept in `app.ts` memory. All cart operations go through one queued
  mutation, so they apply in order; the displayed cart is the latest reply's `cart`. A transport
  failure on a cart operation shows the alert "Check your connection and try again." (the spec
  defines alerts only for `userErrors`). The alert's title is "Couldn’t update cart"; its
  message is the first `userErrors` message.
- **Add to cart.** The tab switches to Cart when the add's reply arrives without `userErrors`.
  The button is disabled while any cart request is in flight.
- **Product screen.** The round back button is fixed over the top-left corner of the screen
  (it stays reachable when the page scrolls) instead of scrolling away with the carousel.
  The Add to cart bar sits below the scroll area rather than over it. Option pills wrap onto
  more lines when they do not fit. Picking a pill selects the variant matching all current
  options with the new value; if no variant has that combination, the first variant with the
  picked value.
- **Collection screen.** The navigation bar, description and sort chips stay fixed; the product
  grid below them is the scrolling container (`product-grid`), a virtualized list of rows of
  two cards. The sort chips scroll horizontally when they do not fit. The title shows the
  collection's title from Home while the collection loads.
- **Home.** The "See all" link in the design is not in the spec and is omitted. The header
  scrolls with the content ("the whole screen scrolls").
- **Errors.** A failed first page shows the full error state; a failed later page (collection,
  search) shows an inline "Couldn’t load products" with Retry at the end of the list, keeping
  the loaded rows.
- **Search.** Shows a spinner while the first page of a query loads. "1 result" is singular.
- **Empty cart.** "Start shopping" switches to the Home tab.
- **Status bar / dark mode.** Colors are the design's fixed light palette on every system theme.

## What could not be met, and why

See the end of `BUILD.md` for toolchain caveats. Items:

- (filled in below as verification finds them)

## Building an app

    bun scripts/agent-android.mjs build caltrain --apk

It needs the Android SDK (`ANDROID_HOME`, else `~/Library/Android/sdk` or `~/Android/Sdk`) with platform 37.2 and an
NDK (`ANDROID_NDK_HOME`, else the newest under the SDK), a JDK (17 or newer) and the Rust target
(`rustup target add aarch64-linux-android`). It:

1. builds the app's `android/` crate for `aarch64-linux-android` at `host-dev` (`--release`: at `release` with fat
   LTO, as a production build links, for measuring). The crate is a cdylib whose source is `exact_linux::canvas_jni!(<the data source>, hatches =
   crate::exact_hatches())`, with a build script that bakes the plan and calls `contract::native::android_entry`,
   which writes the app's hatches' install (`hatches.rs`) and the plan's uses (`uses.txt`) beside it; `apps/caltrain/android` is the one to copy for an app whose data is Rust and
   `apps/shelf/android` for one whose data is TypeScript (three files each, and a line in the root `Cargo.toml`'s
   `members`). A game's is generated in its `.shells/` (`game/app/shells.mjs`). An app with a GPU module (LLP 1009;
   every game) is built as a Linux bake is (`buildBake`): the module first, then the crate, whose bake records the
   module's product digest. The shared Linux/Android loader checks baked cards against that digest: on
   macOS, signed 64-bit Mach-O code omits the signature and normalizes its three size fields, matching
   the definition in `update/src/gpu.rs` through a parity-tested host copy; other files hash whole. Completed development receipts always
   bind the whole file. Both the process cache and Android's persistent cache distinguish these digests;
2. copies the library to `app/build/<app>/rust/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libexactcanvas.so`, the GPU module beside it under
   its own name, the app's `assets/` to `app/build/<app>/rust/assets/app/assets/`, and a GPU module's shaders
   (`gpu/shaders/*.wgsl`, as a Linux bake packs them) to `app/build/<app>/rust/assets/app/shaders/`, where the host
   registers them from before a canvas is made;
3. runs `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease -Papp=<app> -PappDir=<the app's directory>` here (a game's `.shells/`, whose
   `app.json` is resolved), with `-PgpuModule=<file>` for a module: the APK then extracts its libraries and leaves
   the module unstripped, since the host opens it by path and checks its digest; with `-Pcompose=1` when the plan's
   uses name `dates` (a date or time control), which links Compose Material 3 for its pickers; and with the Kotlin
   in the app's `modules/android`, its hatches and module roster, compiled in,

and prints the APK's path. Each build has its own Gradle output and locks: the
shell's build directory (`-PappBuildDir`), the reader's (`-PcanvasBuildDir`), Gradle's project cache
(`--project-cache-dir`) and Kotlin's session files, under `app/build/<app>`, `canvas/build/<app>`, `.gradle/apps/<app>`
and `.kotlin/apps/<app>` for an app of this repository and under the app's own `target/android/` for one outside it, so
builds of two apps at once do not wait on each other or mix outputs. The library is stripped with the NDK it was linked
with (`-PndkPath`). Beside the APK, `exact-build.json` records when the build began, the library and the Kotlin it
compiled: a drive refuses an APK older than its sources by it. `--install` then installs the APK on the device a drive
would use (`--run`: and launches it). The package id and the label are the app's
`app.json` (`app.id`, with `-` as `_`, which a package name cannot hold; `app.name`). `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_idSuffix=.dev` in the environment builds a side-by-side package
(`<app id>.dev`). `./gradlew :canvas:assembleRelease` builds the reader alone.

A component fixture may compile the real app's Kotlin with
`ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_modulesDir=<absolute path to the app's modules/android>`. The default
is the built app's own `modules/android`; this override avoids copying a provider into fixtures.

Then `adb install -r <apk>` and `adb shell am start -n <app id>/dev.exact.app.MainActivity`, or drive it:

input.command:
cd /Users/itome/shopbench-runs/exact/scripts && cat > build-ios-simulator.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Everbloom for the iOS Simulator in release (production) mode: Exact's `ios --release`,
# the build that ships, for the simulator. Result: build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$ROOT/everbloom"
OUT="$ROOT/build/ios-simulator"
BUN="${BUN:-$HOME/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun}"
export PATH="$(dirname "$BUN"):$PATH"

# Builds, and installs on the booted iPhone simulator (or EXACT_SIM / --sim).
(cd "$APP_DIR" && "$BUN" exact.mjs ios --release "$@")

BUILT="$(ls -td "$APP_DIR"/target/clients/*/dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact/ios-simulator/*/*/production/standalone/Everbloom.app | head -1)"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
rm -rf "$OUT/Everbloom.app"
ditto "$BUILT" "$OUT/Everbloom.app"
echo "$OUT/Everbloom.app"
EOF
cat > build-android.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Everbloom's Android release APK (Rust at the release profile, Gradle assembleRelease, debug-signed).
# SHOP_API_URL, if set when this runs, is the endpoint the APK uses.
# Result: build/android/Everbloom-release.apk
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$ROOT/everbloom"
OUT="$ROOT/build/android"
BUN="${BUN:-$HOME/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun}"
export PATH="$(dirname "$BUN"):$PATH"
export ANDROID_HOME="${ANDROID_HOME:-$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}"
if [[ -z "${JAVA_HOME:-}" && -d "/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home" ]]; then
  export JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home"
fi

(cd "$APP_DIR" && EXACT_APP_DIR="$APP_DIR" "$BUN" "$ROOT/vendor/exact2/scripts/agent-android.mjs" build everbloom --apk --release)

mkdir -p "$OUT"
cp "$APP_DIR/target/android/app/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk" "$OUT/Everbloom-release.apk"
echo "$OUT/Everbloom-release.apk"
EOF
cat > install.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Installs what the builds need: the pinned Exact and Ibex checkouts, Bun 1.4.2,
# Exact's toolchains, the app's packages and the Android Hermes bundle.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
EXACT_COMMIT=fc14919528fb76ca8de3e8c8d9ef91853f923a17
IBEX_COMMIT=a0183568e8229b8243629cdb26cd4a88ac4e2abd

fetch() { # <dir> <url> <commit>
  if [[ ! -d "$1/.git" ]]; then git init -q "$1" && git -C "$1" remote add origin "$2"; fi
  if [[ "$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" != "$3" ]]; then
    git -C "$1" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$3" && git -C "$1" checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD
  fi
}
fetch "$ROOT/vendor/exact2" https://github.com/expo/exact.git "$EXACT_COMMIT"
fetch "$ROOT/vendor/ibex" https://github.com/expo/ibex.git "$IBEX_COMMIT"

BUN="$HOME/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun"
if [[ ! -x "$BUN" ]]; then curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | BUN_INSTALL="$HOME/.bun-1.4.2" bash -s bun-v1.4.2; fi
export PATH="$HOME/.bun-1.4.2/bin:$PATH"

(cd "$ROOT/vendor/exact2" && bun scripts/exact.mjs setup)
rustup target add --toolchain 1.97.0 aarch64-apple-ios aarch64-apple-ios-sim aarch64-linux-android
(cd "$ROOT/everbloom" && bun install --frozen-lockfile)

# Android's Hermes bundle (no Ibex release ships one): built once from the Ibex checkout.

# Building Everbloom (Exact)

All commands run from the project root on macOS (Apple silicon). The app is in `everbloom/`;
Exact itself is cloned into `vendor/exact2/` by step 1 (Exact has no releases: an app builds
against a checkout, by path).

> **iOS needs Xcode 27.** The pinned Exact commit (and every public Exact commit) compiles its
> UIKit host against the iOS 27 SDK (`UIArrangementViewController`, iOS 27 `AVAudioSession`
> notifications, Swift 6.3+ features). With Xcode 26.x the Swift compile of `ExactKit` fails.
> If Xcode 27 is not `xcode-select`'s, point the commands at it:
> `export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.app/Contents/Developer`.
> See `NOTES.md`: on the machine this was written on only Xcode 26.6 was installed, so the
> iOS builds below were not run to completion there.

## 1. Install dependencies

Prerequisites: Xcode 27 (with an iOS 27 Simulator runtime), `rustup`, `git`, `curl`, and for
Android the Android SDK (`ANDROID_HOME`, default `~/Library/Android/sdk`) with an NDK and a JDK 17+
(Android Studio's bundled JBR is picked up automatically).

```sh
scripts/install.sh
```

It clones Exact (`expo/exact` at `fc14919528fb76ca8de3e8c8d9ef91853f923a17`) and Ibex
(`expo/ibex` at `a0183568e8229b8243629cdb26cd4a88ac4e2abd`) into `vendor/`, installs Bun 1.4.2
into `~/.bun-1.4.2` (beside any other Bun), runs Exact's `setup` (pinned Rust 1.97.0, Hermes
bundles for macOS and iOS, offline crates), adds the Rust targets `aarch64-apple-ios`,
`aarch64-apple-ios-sim` and `aarch64-linux-android`, installs the app's package
(`@exact/in-app-browser`, from the Exact checkout), and builds the Android Hermes bundle from
the Ibex checkout (about 10 minutes, once; cached in `~/.cache/exact/hermes-android`). For Android
it also needs the SDK platform 37.2:

```sh
"$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager" "platforms;android-37.2"
```

## 2. iOS device release build (benchmarked)

Signed for a team (automatic signing; the Mac's Xcode must be signed in to an account of that team):

```sh
DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 scripts/build-ios-device.sh
```

Without a team (code signing disabled: the bundle is ad-hoc signed, no profile):

```sh
scripts/build-ios-device.sh
```

Result: **`build/ios-device/Everbloom.app`** (and `build/ios-device/Everbloom.ipa`).

Exact builds the `.app` itself (Cargo, SwiftPM, its own bundler and `codesign`), not through an
Xcode project. With `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set, the script first builds a never-shipped stub Xcode
project (`scripts/signing-stub/`) with the same bundle id and `-allowProvisioningUpdates`, so Xcode's
automatic signing creates the team's development profile, then runs Exact's device release build
signed with that profile and the team's Apple Development identity
(`bun exact.mjs ios --device --release --archive …` with `EXACT_PROFILE`/`EXACT_IDENTITY`).
Without it, it runs the same build with `--unsigned`. The first build takes 10–15 minutes.

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
DEVICE=$(xcrun devicectl list devices | awk '/connected/ {print $3; exit}')   # or the phone's UDID / name
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" build/ios-device/Everbloom.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" \
  --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
  dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact
```

Omit `--environment-variables` to use `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`. The app reads
`SHOP_API_URL` from its launch environment (through its Swift module, `everbloom/modules/apple/Shop.swift`).

## 4. iOS Simulator build

Boot an iPhone simulator first (`xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 17 Pro"`; or set `EXACT_SIM` to a
name or UDID). Then:

```sh
scripts/build-ios-simulator.sh
```

Result: **`build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app`** (the script also installs it on the booted simulator).
Install and launch with the endpoint override:

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api xcrun simctl launch booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact
```

The marker line: `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'`.

`scripts/dev-proxy.ts` (`~/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun scripts/dev-proxy.ts 8787`) is a stand-in for the replay
server that forwards to mock.shop; stop it to see the error state, start it again and tap Retry.

## 5. Android release APK

```sh
scripts/build-android.sh                                            # default endpoint
SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api scripts/build-android.sh  # endpoint fixed at build time
```

Result: **`build/android/Everbloom-release.apk`** (`everbloom/target/android/app/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`).

```sh
adb install -r build/android/Everbloom-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact/dev.exact.app.MainActivity
```

The endpoint is read at build time (`app.json` `env`: `SHOP_API_URL` from the environment, else
`everbloom/.env.local`, else `everbloom/.env`) and inlined into the data module. Plain HTTP is
allowed: Exact's `fetch` on Android uses its own Rust sockets, which Android's cleartext policy does
not govern, and the app's grants admit `http:` and `https:` to any host.

## 6. Build modes and toolchains

| Build | Mode |
|---|---|
| iOS device | Exact production: `ios --device --release --archive` (Rust `release` profile, Swift whole-module `-O`, `EXACT_UPDATE_TRUST=production`, plan and Hermes bytecode baked in, no development server, no agent, no hot reload, no dev menu; update store `"0"`, so no update checks) |
| iOS Simulator | The same production mode for the simulator: `ios --release` (Exact's "build that ships", the most production-like it offers on the simulator) |
| Android | Rust `release` profile (fat LTO) + Gradle `assembleRelease`, signed with the debug key |

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| Exact | `expo/exact` `fc14919528fb76ca8de3e8c8d9ef91853f923a17` (2026-11-10) |
| Bun | 1.4.2 (pinned by Exact) |
| Rust | 1.97.0 (pinned by Exact's `rust-toolchain.toml`) |
| Hermes | 260318099.0.4 (Ibex bundle `hermes-vanilla-d412d3bd8512-v5`; Android built from Ibex `a0183568`) |
| Xcode | 27 required (iOS 27 SDK); this machine had 26.6 (17F113), which fails |
| Android | SDK platform 37.2, NDK 29.0.14206865, Gradle 9.8.0 (wrapper), JDK 21 (Android Studio JBR), CMake 3.22.1 (SDK) for Hermes |
| macOS | 26 (Darwin 25.5) |

Xcode project. With `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set, the script first builds a never-shipped stub Xcode
project (`scripts/signing-stub/`) with the same bundle id and `-allowProvisioningUpdates`, so Xcode's
automatic signing creates the team's development profile, then runs Exact's device release build
signed with that profile and the team's Apple Development identity
(`bun exact.mjs ios --device --release --archive …` with `EXACT_PROFILE`/`EXACT_IDENTITY`).
Without it, it runs the same build with `--unsigned`. The first build takes 10–15 minutes.

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
DEVICE=$(xcrun devicectl list devices | awk '/connected/ {print $3; exit}')   # or the phone's UDID / name
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" build/ios-device/Everbloom.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" \
  --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
  dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact
```

Omit `--environment-variables` to use `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`. The app reads
`SHOP_API_URL` from its launch environment (through its Swift module, `everbloom/modules/apple/Shop.swift`).

## 4. iOS Simulator build

Boot an iPhone simulator first (`xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 17 Pro"`; or set `EXACT_SIM` to a
name or UDID). Then:

```sh
scripts/build-ios-simulator.sh
```

Result: **`build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app`** (the script also installs it on the booted simulator).
Install and launch with the endpoint override:

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api xcrun simctl launch booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact
```

The marker line: `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'`.

`scripts/dev-proxy.ts` (`~/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun scripts/dev-proxy.ts 8787`) is a stand-in for the replay
server that forwards to mock.shop; stop it to see the error state, start it again and tap Retry.

## 5. Android release APK

```sh
scripts/build-android.sh                                            # default endpoint
SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api scripts/build-android.sh  # endpoint fixed at build time
```

Result: **`build/android/Everbloom-release.apk`** (`everbloom/target/android/app/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`).

```sh
adb install -r build/android/Everbloom-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact/dev.exact.app.MainActivity
```

The endpoint is read at build time (`app.json` `env`: `SHOP_API_URL` from the environment, else
`everbloom/.env.local`, else `everbloom/.env`) and inlined into the data module. Plain HTTP is
allowed: Exact's `fetch` on Android uses its own Rust sockets, which Android's cleartext policy does
not govern, and the app's grants admit `http:` and `https:` to any host.

## 6. Build modes and toolchains

| Build | Mode |
|---|---|
| iOS device | Exact production: `ios --device --release --archive` (Rust `release` profile, Swift whole-module `-O`, `EXACT_UPDATE_TRUST=production`, plan and Hermes bytecode baked in, no development server, no agent, no hot reload, no dev menu; update store `"0"`, so no update checks) |
| iOS Simulator | The same production mode for the simulator: `ios --release` (Exact's "build that ships", the most production-like it offers on the simulator) |
| Android | Rust `release` profile (fat LTO) + Gradle `assembleRelease`, signed with the debug key |

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|

| Bun | 1.4.2 (pinned by Exact) |
| Rust | 1.97.0 (pinned by Exact's `rust-toolchain.toml`) |
| Hermes | 260318099.0.4 (Ibex bundle `hermes-vanilla-d412d3bd8512-v5`; Android built from Ibex `a0183568`) |
| Xcode | 27 required (iOS 27 SDK); this machine had 26.6 (17F113), which fails |
| Android | SDK platform 37.2, NDK 29.0.14206865, Gradle 9.8.0 (wrapper), JDK 21 (Android Studio JBR), CMake 3.22.1 (SDK) for Hermes |
| macOS | 26 (Darwin 25.5) |

content.text:
I built the Everbloom app with Exact, but it can't be built or run for iOS on this machine. Current Exact needs Xcode 27 (the iOS 27 SDK), and only Xcode 26.6 is installed here; with 26.6, compiling Exact's own iOS code fails. So none of the iOS items in the Done list are met yet: the device and simulator builds, the simulator walkthrough, the `SHOPBENCH home_ready` log line, and the accessibility IDs as seen by XCUITest.

I tried to install Xcode 27.2 from the App Store, but that asks for an admin password, which I don't have. I also didn't want to replace the system Xcode, because the other framework projects on this machine use it. I had briefly made a copy of Xcode 26.6 as a fallback; I deleted it when the install failed, so the system is as it was.

**What I could check:**
- **Web:** I ran the same app code in Exact's web host (headless Chromium, phone-sized window, live mock.shop data). Every flow in the Done list worked, including Retry after the endpoint comes back. Checkout wasn't tried there, and neither was the alert for cart errors.
- **Android:** the release APK builds, launches on the emulator, and Home loads.
- **Tests:** the 3 tests in `everbloom/app.test.contract` pass on the web host. They cover the loading skeleton, tabs, empty search, empty cart and the error state.

**What's untested:**
- The iOS build scripts follow Exact's documented commands but haven't run end to end.
- For `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` signing, Exact builds the app without an Xcode project. The script therefore first builds a dummy Xcode project with the same bundle ID, so Xcode creates the team's provisioning profile, then has Exact sign with it. That dummy project builds with signing off; the signed path has never run.

**Next step:** install Xcode 27 with admin rights (in parallel with Xcode 26.6 if the other projects need it), set `DEVELOPER_DIR` to point at it, and run `scripts/build-ios-simulator.sh`. After that I can do the simulator walkthrough and check the log line. iOS layout specifics such as safe areas haven't been seen on a real iOS build yet, so I'd expect a round of fixes there.

**How it's laid out:**
- **App folder:** the app is in `everbloom/`, not the project root. Exact names its build pieces after the folder, and `exact` clashes with Exact's own names, so it refused to create the app at the root.
- **Exact and Ibex:** both are cloned into `vendor/` at pinned commits by `scripts/install.sh`, and Exact isn't modified. Ibex is Expo's Hermes repo; Android needs a Hermes build that no Ibex release ships yet, and the build takes about 10 minutes, once.
- **Endpoint:** on iOS, `SHOP_API_URL` is read at launch by a small Swift module, which also writes the `os_log` line. On Android it's read at build time.
- **Plain HTTP on Android:** it needed no setting. Exact makes requests over its own sockets, which Android's cleartext policy doesn't govern.
- **Dependency:** the only one added is Exact's own `@exact/in-app-browser`, used for Check out.
- **Extra machine setup:** to build, I installed Playwright's Chromium, Bun 1.4.2, the Android SDK platform 37.2, and the Rust iOS targets.

All my decisions where the spec is silent, plus the Xcode blocker, are in `NOTES.md`.

Files are in `/Users/itome/shopbench-runs/exact`:
- `BUILD.md`
- `NOTES.md`
- `build/android/Everbloom-release.apk`
